records.description:
**About Komline**

As a pioneering leader in advanced separation technologies, Komline has established a global reputation for engineering excellence. Through our combination of innovative design, cutting-edge manufacturing capabilities, and decades of industry experience, we consistently deliver the highest quality equipment from our integrated manufacturing facilities. Serving our core markets of Water & Process, Agricultural & Renewables, and Industrials, we pride ourselves on providing comprehensive separation solutions precisely tailored to our clients' requirements. With a strong track record of strategic growth and acquisitions, Komline continues to expand its solution portfolio and technical capabilities while maintaining our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction.

**This Opportunity**

The Director, Operational Excellence is responsible for building, deploying, and sustaining the Komline Business System (KBS), a consistent operating excellence system across all Komline sites. This leader will partner with Business Unit General Managers, Plant Managers, and functional leaders to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, working capital, productivity, and overall operating discipline while respecting the P&L accountability of each business. The role will lead Komline’s enterprise continuous improvement (CI) capability, develop CI talent, and ensure proven practices are shared and scaled across the network.

The successful candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who combines strong Lean expertise with business judgment, credibility on the shop floor, and the executive presence to influence decentralized business leaders. This leader will be equally comfortable coaching a plant team, challenging a site improvement plan, and communicating enterprise priorities to senior leadership.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this enterprise-wide role supports all Komline operating sites.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

* Develop and lead implementation of the KBS Operational Excellence strategy, roadmap, standards, and multi-year improvement agenda across all sites
* Lead, coach, and develop the CI Manager team and other improvement resources; establish clear site coverage, priorities, and deployment expectations
* Partner with GMs and Plant Managers to identify the highest-impact opportunities and build robust, financially validated site-level improvement pipelines that deliver sustained results in safety, productivity, delivery, lead time, quality, inventory, cost, and working capital
* Establish and sustain common Lean / KBS operating practices, including daily management, visual management, standard work, problem solving, RCCM, value-stream improvement, kaizen, and leader standard work
* Create a practical maturity assessment for Operational Excellence and use it to prioritize coaching, capability building, and site support; track improvements in maturity and consistent adoption of core operating practices
* Drive measurable productivity and capacity improvements through flow, labor optimization, constraint removal, setup reduction, layout improvement, and waste elimination
* Partner with Industrial Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, EHS, Finance, Engineering, HR, and other enterprise functions to quantify benefits and ensure improvements are sustained
* Build CI capability within site leadership and frontline teams through training, coaching, kaizen leadership, and development of local change agents
* Establish common operational KPI definitions and review routines that enable benchmarking and the sharing and scaling of best practices across Komline
* Support acquisition integration by assessing operational maturity, identifying improvement opportunities, and integrating acquired sites into Komline’s operating system
* Provide regular enterprise-level reporting to the COO on CI pipeline, benefits realization, site maturity, risks, and resource priorities
* Promote a culture of accountability, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement while maintaining strong partnership with decentralized business leadership

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, operational excellence, industrial engineering, or related leadership roles
* Demonstrated success leading Lean / continuous improvement across multiple sites or business units
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, daily management, kaizen, standard work, value-stream mapping, structured problem solving, and performance management
* Proven ability to influence GMs, Plant Managers, and functional leaders without relying on direct authority
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to translate operational improvements into measurable financial impact
* Excellent leadership, coaching, facilitation, communication, and executive presentation skills
* Ability to travel approximately 50%+, depending on site and project needs

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Lean leadership certification or equivalent and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt
* Experience in multi-site industrial, engineered-product, capital-equipment, or process-equipment manufacturing
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or deploying a common operating system across decentralized businesses
* Experience with plant layout, flow optimization, capacity improvement, and working-capital initiatives
* MBA or advanced technical/operations degree

records.title: Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering
records.description:
**Job Summary**
The Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering is a hands-on leadership role and the process authority for how Butcher Power Products’ switchboard and switchgear products are built. The person in this role must be the subject-matter expert who can also do the work — capable of designing and improving manufacturing processes and line layouts, building routings and process documentation, and personally leading process and PFMEA reviews — so they can teach and develop the manufacturing engineering team and set the standard for process quality. This role owns how products are built rather than what is designed; however, deep familiarity with the product and the production floor is essential. The Director must understand the design intent released by Product Engineering and the realities of the floor in order to engineer processes that are efficient, repeatable, and capable. This role works hand in hand with Product Engineering as the manufacturing voice in the design process, partners with Quality on process controls, and supports Production and Planning rather than owning them.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Hands-On Process Engineering: Personally design, document, and improve the manufacturing processes, routings, work instructions, and line layouts that build the product. This is a working role: the successful candidate stays actively engaged in process design and technical problem-solving alongside the team rather than delegating all hands-on work.
* Process Authority & Technical Review: Lead, critique, and approve the team’s process designs, routings, PFMEAs, and control plans; set and enforce the standard for process quality, capability, and engineering rigor through formal process reviews.
* Mentorship & Teaching: Coach, train, and develop manufacturing engineers and technicians in process design, tooling, DFM/DFA, Lean and Six Sigma, time studies, and structured problem-solving, raising the technical capability of the whole team.
* Leadership & Management: Lead and manage the manufacturing engineering team, including hiring, development, workload balancing, priorities, and performance.
* Process Strategy & Standardization: Own manufacturing process strategy and standardization across product lines, and define the tooling and capital equipment roadmap.
* Product Engineering Partnership (DFM): Work closely and continuously with Product Engineering as the manufacturing voice in the design process — provide manufacturability and assembly feedback at design reviews before release, jointly resolve producibility issues, and ensure released designs transition cleanly into production.
* Process Controls & Quality Partnership: Own the manufacturing side of PFMEAs and control plans in partnership with Quality Engineering; ensure processes are capable, controlled, and continuously monitored.
* Continuous Improvement: Drive Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen across the function to improve throughput, cycle time, yield, and cost.
* Capital, Tooling & Automation: Plan and justify capital equipment, tooling, and automation investments, and provide financial management of the manufacturing engineering capital and tooling budgets.
* New Product Introduction (NPI): Lead the process side of NPI — develop and validate the processes, tooling, and routings that bring newly released designs into production.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Production, Planning, Quality, Project Management, and Product Engineering on capacity, scheduling, and material flow, supporting these functions rather than owning them.
* Safety & Compliance: Ensure manufacturing processes across the function comply with safety, environmental, and regulatory standards, including UL 891, NEC, and ANSI.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Industrial, or Mechanical Engineering.
* 8+ years of progressive process engineering (or directly related) experience, including significant time spent personally developing and improving manufacturing processes.
* Hands-on proficiency in SolidWorks for process documentation, line layouts, and reviews; the ability to design tooling and fixtures in CAD is a plus.
* Strong proficiency developing routings, work instructions, process documentation, and process controls.
* Proven ability to lead formal process and PFMEA reviews and to mentor and train engineers and technicians.
* Experience hiring, developing, and managing a manufacturing engineering team.
* Strong working knowledge of PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and process capability (Cpk).
* Deep knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Strong understanding of the products being built and of how design intent translates into manufacturing process — sufficient product familiarity to engineer the right processes.
* Working knowledge of UL 891 and related standards (NEC, ANSI) as they affect manufacturing processes.
* Experience planning and justifying capital equipment and tooling investments, including financial management of budgets.
* Hands-on fabrication and machining experience is a plus.
* Automation experience is a plus.
* Experience with structured problem-solving methods such as 8D or A3 is a plus.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, particularly Microsoft Dynamics 365 (D365).
* Excellent leadership, project management, and problem-solving skills.
* Strong communication and interpersonal abilities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Hands-on manufacturing process design and improvement (CAD)
* Process authority and engineering quality standards
* Technical mentoring, teaching, and team development
* Close partnership with Product Engineering (DFM)
* Process strategy, standardization, and tooling roadmap
* Design-for-manufacturability partnership
* Process controls, PFMEA, and capability
* Continuous improvement and Lean/Six Sigma
* Capital planning, automation, and financial management
* New product introduction (process side)
* Cross-functional collaboration and communication

**Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering**

**Location:**
Rancho Cordova, CA (Onsite)

**Employment Type:**
Full-Time, Permanent

**Compensation:**
Up to $225,000 annually

**Start Date:**
ASAP

**Position Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on
**Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering**
to lead and develop a manufacturing engineering team within an established electrical equipment manufacturing operation in Rancho Cordova, California.

records.title: Sr. Manager, Optimus Operations
records.description:
**What To Expect**
The Senior Manager, Optimus Operations sets the vision and strategic path for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering within a major shop at Tesla’s new Optimus Factory in Austin, Texas. Openings span operations leadership across multiple shops—including Plastics, Machining, Actuators, and Assembly. Each role leads their shop teams and cross-functional partners to achieve Safety, People, Quality, Production/Delivery, and Cost KPI targets.
 
 
This role is responsible for production and resource planning; coaching, mentoring, and developing leaders; launching new Optimus manufacturing processes and programs successfully; and daily tactical planning and execution to achieve the build plan and meet safety, quality, rate, and cost targets. The person in this role must guide the team through complex issues, distill large volumes of data to solve problems, and drive day-over-day continuous improvement in a high-volume, high-precision factory environment.
 
 
This Senior Manager provides hands-on support, leadership, and direction on all operational, team morale, and equipment-related matters. The person in this role builds teams that work cohesively and perform at the highest level—keeping Tesla’s mission and the goals of the Optimus program in mind—while partnering closely with peer shop leaders and factory leadership across the Austin Optimus Factory.
 
 
**What You'll Do**- Set the vision and strategic path for Production and Maintenance in an assigned Optimus shop and lead the team to Safety, People, Quality, Production, and Cost KPI targets
- Drive tactical planning to hit the production build plan with the highest safety, quality, and yield, including identifying bottlenecks and addressing availability, efficiency, and yield constraints
- Launch new Optimus programs and lead production ramps and product/process design changes through resource planning, program management, and partnership with NPI, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain
- Guide the team through root cause analysis, first-principles thinking, and data-driven problem solving while maintaining standardized work and quality/safety compliance
- Coach, mentor, and develop Production, Maintenance, and Engineering leaders, instill process standardization and training, and drive continuous improvement
- Lead the maintenance organization on equipment availability, preventive and predictive maintenance, spare parts strategy, and uptime improvements for shop-critical assets
- Build a high-performing team with clear goals and feedback, improve morale with HR, and collaborate with peer shop Senior Managers to share best practices
**What You'll Bring**- Degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Materials, or Industrial Engineering preferred, or equivalent experience
- 7–10 years of leadership and manufacturing experience, preferably in automotive, robotics, plastics, precision machining, electromechanical assembly/actuators, general assembly, or another highly technical manufacturing environment
- Analytical, detail-oriented, self-driven critical thinker who communicates proactively and works well in a fast-paced, multicultural factory environment
- Experience with process-improvement methodologies, DOE/statistical methods, lean and world-class manufacturing practices, and standing up or ramping new factories, shops, or production lines
- Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to work under pressure, juggle competing priorities, and meet tight deadlines
- Ability to use structured problem-solving methods such as 8D, fishbone diagrams, and 5-Why analysis to resolve production problems
- High-level leadership and decision-making skills with a strong sense of urgency in a greenfield/new-factory ramp, plus proficiency in MS Office, Visio, CAD, SPC, data-analysis tools, Jira, Tableau/BI dashboards, and project-management tools
**Benefits**
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
 
- Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
- Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
- Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
- Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
- Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
- 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
- Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
- Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
- Employee Assistance Program
- Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
- Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
- Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
- Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
- Tesla Babies program
- Commuter benefits
- Employee discounts and perks program
- Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)
, Tesla

records.title: R&D NPI Engineering Senior Manager, Project Management

postedPay.title: R&D NPI Engineering Senior Manager, Project Management

records.description:
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.

**What You Will Experience In This Position**

The R&D NPI Engineering Senior Manager will be a strategic and hands-on leader who drives on-time delivery and best practices for our new product introduction (NPI) programs within our Data Solutions business. This role will lead, coach and mentor a team of project and program managers to ensure alignment with business goals through effective portfolio and process management. The manager will work closely with business unit leaders, product managers, and engineering leaders to drive and improve on-time delivery and cross-functional collaboration for our portfolio of NPI programs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Team Leadership & Development:**
Lead, mentor and inspire a high-performing, global project management team specializing in NPI Program execution. Develop a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and empower the team to drive excellence in project delivery.

**NPI Execution and Delivery:**
Oversee end-to-end execution of projects, ensuring on-time delivery, within scope and on budget while maintaining high quality outcomes.

**Cross-Functional Coordination:**
Partner closely with engineering, product management, integrated supply chain, manufacturing and operations teams to ensure alignment of project priorities, resources, and timelines, facilitating seamless execution of programs.

**Resource Allocation:**
Optimize resource planning and allocation across projects, balancing capacity dynamically to meet changing business priorities and ensure effective utilization

**Portfolio Management:**
Collaborate with key partners to drive the selection and prioritization of NPI projects, connected to our strategic objectives and business goals.

**Continuous Improvement**
: Own and evolve the NPI phase-gate process to ensure consistent and efficient product development lifecycle execution. Drive continuous evaluation and enhancement of our project management processes, tools and methodologies to improve efficiency and scalability of programs.

**Performance & Reporting:**
Define and track KPIs to measure project health and business impact. Lead monthly business reviews to communicate progress, risks, and opportunities to senior leadership.

**You Have**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering
* Ideally 10+ years of proven experience in NPI or PMO leadership roles, preferably in data or technology-driven environments of which 2+ years of people leadership experience, including coaching, mentoring, and developing high-performing teams
* Proven record of leading large-scale, complex projects and driving successful product introductions
* Proficiency in demonstrating expertise in PMO practices, methodologies, tools and processes.
* Outstanding ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams and drive results in a matrixed organization.
* Excellent communication, coaching, and stakeholder management skills.
* Strong analytical, problem solving and decision-making abilities to drive efficiency and optimize project outcomes.
* Experience in manufacturing, industrial, or engineering focused organizations

**We Have**

* A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day
* nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.
* Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com.
* Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work
* We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide
* Through our nVent in Action matching program, we provide funds to nonprofit and educational organizations where our employees volunteer or donate money

Core values that shape our culture and drive us to deliver the best for our employees and our customers. We’re known for being:

* Innovative & adaptable
* Dedicated to absolute integrity
* Focused on the customer first
* Respectful and team oriented
* Optimistic and energizing
* Accountable for performance
* Benefits to support the lives of our employees

**Pay Transparency**

nVent’s pay scale is based on the expected range of base pay for this job and the employee’s work location. Employee pay within this range will be based on a combination of factors including knowledge, skills, abilities, experience, education, and performance. Where federal, state, or local minimum wage requirements exist, employee pay will comply.

**Compensation Range**

$123,500.00 - $229,500.00

Depending on the position offered, employee may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as annual incentives.

**Benefit Overview**

At nVent, we value our people and their health and well-being. We provide a broad benefits package with meaningful programs for eligible full-time employees that includes:

* Medical, dental, and vision plans along with flexible spending accounts, short-term and long-term disability benefits, critical illness, accident insurance and life insurance.
* A 401(k) retirement plan and an employee stock purchase plan — both include a company match.
* Other supplemental benefits may include tuition reimbursement, caregiver, personal and parental leave, back-up care services, paid time off including volunteer time, a well-being program, and/or legal & identity theft protection.

At nVent, we connect and protect our customers with inventive electrical solutions. People are our most valuable asset. Inclusion and diversity means that we celebrate and encourage each other’s authenticity because we understand that uniqueness sparks growth.

records.title: Director, Value Stream Manufacturing
records.description:
**Director, Manufacturing Value Stream**
Global Value Stream As a Director on the Global Value Stream team, you will
*lead*
our Manufacturing value stream within HelloFresh's global supply chain, shaping the strategy and execution model for how we standardize, improve, and scale our operations worldwide. You will lead a team, set the department's operational agenda, and serve as a senior voice of operations across the organization. This is a high-impact leadership role that sits at the intersection of operations, technology, and global strategy.
 
 
***You will...***

* Define and execute the strategic direction for the portfolio of Manufacturing processes, owning the multi-year capability roadmap and global template.
* Lead and build a high-performing, accountable department with clear OKRs aligned to company strategy.
* Set the governance framework and operating model for how the Global Value Stream team designs, validates, and deploys process and technology standards internationally.
* Partner at the executive level with Operations, Product, Engineering, and others to align on global priorities, technology investments, and performance benchmarks.
* Serve as the final decision authority on process deviation requests, capability exceptions, and cross-market design trade-offs.
* Drive the organization's approach to continuous improvement, value stream analysis, and waste elimination at scale — setting the standard for how the company approaches process maturity.
* Ensure the team functions as an effective internal consultancy — providing rigorous expert support to regional operations, quality teams, and technology partners.

***You have...***

* 12–15+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, operations, or manufacturing — including significant senior leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading multi-functional teams across multiple geographies, with full accountability for operational outcomes.
* Deep expertise across multiple supply chain functional domains, with a breadth of experience that enables credible leadership across the full Value Stream portfolio.
* Strong commercial acumen and experience managing department budgets and delivering measurable business impact.
* Extensive experience with global process standardization, operational technology ecosystems (WMS/WES/WCS/automation), and large-scale transformation programs.
* A track record of developing senior talent and building high-performance organizations.
* Experience operating as a senior stakeholder in cross-functional governance and product/technology lifecycle processes.
* Ability to travel up to 25%

***You are...***

* A bold, strategic leader with the operational depth to earn the trust of both warehouse teams and the C-suite.
* Comfortable navigating ambiguity at the department level while maintaining clarity and pace for your team.
* A talent multiplier — known for developing strong leaders and creating organizations that outlast any individual.
* A rigorous, data-driven decision maker who moves fast without sacrificing quality or thoroughness.
* Passionate about building world-class operations at scale — energized by the complexity and impact of a global mandate.
* An outstanding communicator and influencer who can drive alignment across diverse cultures, functions, and levels of seniority.

**Additionally With This Role, You Will Have....**

* The opportunity to shape global operations at a leading food technology company with significant reach and impact.
* A high-ownership, low-bureaucracy environment where your work is visible and your decisions matter.
* Flexible working arrangements to support your work-life balance.
* Continuous development through HelloFresh Academies and access to internal mobility across 18 countries.
* An egoless, collaborative culture focused on learning, growth, and building something exceptional together.

***You’ll get…***

* Competitive salary, 401k with company match that vests immediately upon participation
* Generous PTO, including sabbatical, and parental leave of up to 16 weeks
* Comprehensive health and wellness benefits with options at $0 monthly, effective first day of employment
* Tuition reimbursement for continuing education (upon 2 years of service)
* Up to 85% discount on subscriptions to HelloFresh meal plans (HelloFresh, Green Chef, Everyplate, and Factor\_)
* Access to Employee Resource Groups that are open to all employees, including those pertaining to BIPOC, women, veterans, parents, and LGBTQ+
* Inclusive, collaborative, and dynamic work environment within a fast-paced, mission-driven company that is disrupting the traditional food supply chain

This job description is intended to provide a general overview of the responsibilities. However, the Company reserves the right to adjust, modify, or reassign work tasks and responsibilities as needed to meet changing business needs, operational requirements, or other factors.
 
 
**FOR CO POSTINGS**
*Our company is committed to fair hiring practices and complies with all applicable laws, including the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act (JAFA). In accordance with JAFA, we will not request your age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution on your initial application for employment.*
**Education**
*When submitting supporting documents such as a resume, curriculum vitae (CV), or educational transcripts, you may voluntarily redact or omit any information that would identify your age. This includes:*

* Dates of birth
* Dates of attendance at educational institutions
* Dates of graduation

*Your decision to redact this information will not adversely affect the consideration of your application. We evaluate all candidates based on their skills, qualifications, and experience. Please be aware that should you receive a conditional offer of employment, we may be required to request this information for legally permissible purposes, such as verifying eligibility for employment or for benefits administration and background checks.*

records.title: Quality Improvement Director
records.description:
***POSITION PURPOSE:***

The Director of Quality Improvement operates under the leadership and direction of the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) and Chief Operating Officer (COO). The CMO maintains direct clinical oversight of clinical quality improvement activities and regulatory quality programs. The Director of Quality Improvement provides organization-wide leadership for EVCHC's quality improvement program. The Director establishes the quality strategy in partnership with executive, clinical, operational and compliance leaders; converts organizational goals and regulatory requirements into measurable work plans; and leads improvement efforts that strengthen patient outcomes, safety, access, equity and care experience. The Director is accountable for reliable quality data, required clinical quality reporting, continuous improvement methods, Patient Centered Medical Home recognition, and the performance of the Quality Improvement Department.

 

***MAJOR POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES AND FUNCTIONS:***

**Quality Strategy and Governance**

* Lead the development, implementation and annual evaluation of EVCHC's organization-wide Quality Improvement and Quality Assurance Plan in alignment with the strategic plan, clinical standards and applicable Health Center Program requirements.

* Establish annual quality priorities, measures, targets, owners and timelines with executive and clinical leadership. Monitor progress and recommend corrective action when performance does not meet established goals.

* Lead or support the Quality Improvement Committee and related workgroups. Prepare agendas, dashboards, meeting materials, decisions and follow-up reports for executive leadership and the Board of Directors, as requested.

* Advise executive leaders on emerging quality risks, performance trends, resource needs and opportunities to improve care delivery across sites and service lines.

* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, patient safety and learning throughout the organization.

**Department Leadership**

* Direct the work of the Quality Improvement Department, including recruitment, onboarding, supervision, coaching, performance evaluation, workload assignment and staff development.

* Develop departmental goals, staffing plans, procedures and budgets that support timely completion of quality priorities and reporting obligations.

* Set clear expectations for the accuracy, timeliness and usability of analyses, audits, reports and improvement support provided by the department.

* Build effective working relationships with clinical care teams, Operations, Information Technology, Compliance, Human Resources, Finance, Behavioral Health, Dental and other departments involved in quality outcomes.

**Quality Measurement and Reporting**

* Oversee the collection, validation, analysis and submission of clinical quality measures and required reports, including Uniform Data System measures, population health platforms transition and readiness, HEDIS and payer measures, grant measures and internal quality indicators.

* Develop and maintain executive, provider, site and service-line dashboards that show current performance, trends, disparities, targets and improvement actions.

* Track provider and care-team performance, identify variation and care gaps, and provide leaders with actionable information while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and data-use standards.

* Establish data-validation controls and documentation so that quality reports can be reconciled to source systems and used as an organization-wide source of truth. Partnering with Director of Data and IT operations for oversight on data governance committee.

* Present quality findings in clear written and verbal reports to the Board, executive leadership, managers, providers, staff, health plans and external reviewers, as appropriate.

**Performance Improvement**

* Lead Plan Do Study Act cycles, root-cause analyses and other structured improvement methods from problem definition through implementation, evaluation and sustainment.

* Partner with clinical and operational leaders to improve preventive care, chronic disease outcomes, access, continuity, patient experience, care coordination, documentation and other priority measures.

* Translate data findings into practical workflow changes, training, decision support, audit tools and accountability processes that can be sustained across sites.

* Evaluate improvement results, identify lessons learned and spread effective practices to other care teams, programs or locations when appropriate **Regulatory Readiness and Patient Safety**

* Lead the quality components of Patient Centered Medical Home recognition and renewal, including evidence collection, workflow assessment, documentation, staff education and sustainment of recognized practices alongside Director of compliance.

* Partner with Compliance Director, Risk Management, clinical leadership and Operations on quality-related readiness for HRSA operational site visits, FTCA deeming and risk-management activities, health plan audits, accreditation reviews and other external assessments.

* Support corrective action plans with the Director of Compliance arising from audits, quality reviews, safety events or regulatory findings. Define measures, monitor completion and verify that corrective actions are effective and sustained.

* Analyze trends in patient safety events, grievances and quality-of-care concerns with the appropriate leaders while protecting confidentiality and following reporting requirements.

* Maintain organized records of quality plans, committee actions, reports, audits, improvement projects and supporting evidence required for oversight and external review.

**Clinical Analytics and Health Information Technology**

* Direct the clinical analytics program and define reporting requirements that support clinical decision-making, population health management and performance improvement.

* Partner with Information Technology and system vendors to improve data extraction, interfaces, registries, care guidelines, clinical decision support, templates and reporting tools used for quality measurement.

* Lead data-governance practices for quality information, including measure definitions, ownership, validation, access, change control and resolution of reporting discrepancies.

* Assess the quality and workflow impact of new digital tools and automation used in clinical or quality processes and recommend safeguards, testing and performance monitoring before broad implementation.

* Recommend redesign of workflows affected by the electronic health record, patient portal, population health platforms and other clinical information systems.

**Organizational Responsibilities**

* Participate in executive, management, clinical and staff meetings related to quality priorities and organizational performance.

* Maintain current knowledge of FQHC quality requirements, clinical quality measures, health plan expectations and recognized improvement practices.

* Protect patient, employee and organizational information and comply with HIPAA, confidentiality, cybersecurity and records-management requirements.

* Perform other job-related duties as assigned within the scope of the position.

***POSITION REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS:***

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in public health, health care administration, nursing, health sciences, informatics or a related field is required. A master's degree is preferred.

* At least five years of progressive experience in health care quality improvement, population health, clinical analytics or health care program management is required, including at least three years of supervisory or department leadership experience.

* Experience in a Federally Qualified Health Center, community health center or other safety-net setting is strongly preferred.

* Experience leading cross-functional improvement projects and preparing quality reports for executives, governing boards, health plans or regulatory agencies is required.

* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality, Lean or Six Sigma certification, or comparable quality-improvement training is preferred.

**Knowledge and Skills**

* Working knowledge of continuous quality improvement methods, patient safety practices, clinical quality measurement, health equity and population health management.

* Knowledge of HRSA Health Center Program expectations, Uniform Data System reporting, HEDIS measures, Patient Centered Medical Home standards and payer quality programs is strongly preferred.

* Advanced ability to collect, validate, analyze and present health care data and to translate findings into operational decisions and improvement plans.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint and experience using electronic health records, population health platforms, data visualization tools or clinical reporting applications. Experience with NextGen or comparable systems is preferred.

* Strong leadership, project management, facilitation, written communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build accountability across departments .

* Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet reporting deadlines, exercise sound judgment and communicate sensitive performance information professionally.

* Demonstrated commitment to serving medically underserved communities and reducing disparities in access, care and health outcomes.

***WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL/MENTAL ABILITIES AND PROCESSES:***

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

 

* Work is performed primarily in an office and health center environment and requires regular travel among EVCHC sites and occasional travel to meetings or trainings.

* The position requires extended periods of sitting and computer use, as well as standing, walking, bending, reaching, speaking, hearing and seeing sufficient to perform assigned duties.

* The employee must be able to communicate clearly, review detailed reports, maintain concentration, manage competing deadlines and work effectively in shared office and clinical environments.

* The employee must be able to lift and carry materials and equipment weighing up to 20 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

DOE: $125,000 - $148,824 Annually

Please apply to this position with your current resume.

records.description:
*ZetSol Energy | A Zetwerk Company | Solar Manufacturing & Supply Chain Platform for North America*

**Position:** Director – Operations 
**Location:** North Carolina/ South Carolina 
**Type:** Full-Time 
**Reports To:** CEO, ZetSol Energy

**Who We Are**

ZetSol Energy is the solar manufacturing and supply chain platform built to give North American solar developers, EPCs, utilities, and independent power producers a reliable, tariff-compliant alternative to fragmented overseas sourcing. The company is establishing a vertically integrated greenfield facility in Tuticorin, Tamil Nadu, producing silicon ingots, monocrystalline wafers, cells, and modules, including high-efficiency TOPCon and HJT technology, and pairs that manufacturing base with a full strategic sourcing, bill-of-materials management, quality audit, compliance, and logistics practice purpose-built for the US market.

ZetSol Energy is backed by Zetwerk, a global manufacturing platform valued at over $2.7 billion that already supplies solar piles, mechanical and structural components, and modules to leading US EPCs and asset owners, and whose 2022 acquisition of Unimacts strengthened its US industrial and solar manufacturing footprint. ZetSol Energy is the next chapter of that build-out: a dedicated US-facing commercial platform launching at a moment when American solar developers are actively searching for supply chain partners who can deliver both scale and certainty.

**The Opportunity**

We are looking for an experienced operations leader to lead and scale ZetSol Energy's US operations, with overall responsibility for manufacturing, factory production, supply chain, logistics and sales operations.

The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in managing large-scale operations, with a strong background in Supply Chain Management (SCM), logistics and manufacturing, preferably within the renewable energy, solar or industrial sectors.

This individual will be responsible for overseeing factory production, managing end-to-end supply chain and logistics operations, and driving sales operations, including demand planning, order management and customer fulfilment in the US market.

The role will also involve building strong relationships with US government authorities, regulatory bodies, logistics partners and other key industry stakeholders, while ensuring operational efficiency, regulatory compliance and cost optimisation.

This is a key leadership position that will play an instrumental role in building and scaling ZetSol Energy's US operations, establishing robust operational processes and driving business growth in North America.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead and oversee end-to-end US operations for ZetSol Energy, covering manufacturing, supply chain, logistics and sales operations.
* Manage factory production operations, including production planning, capacity utilisation, quality, productivity and timely delivery.
* Drive end-to-end supply chain and logistics operations, including global sourcing, procurement, inventory management, import/export, customs clearance and distribution.
* Oversee sales operations, including demand planning, order management, customer fulfilment and coordination with commercial teams.
* Build and manage relationships with US government authorities, regulatory bodies, customs officials, port authorities, logistics partners and other key stakeholders.
* Ensure compliance with US trade regulations, import policies, tariffs and applicable industry standards while driving operational efficiency and cost optimisation.
* Build and scale the US operations team, processes and infrastructure while working closely with the leadership and manufacturing teams in India.

**Qualifications**

* 15–20 years of experience in operations, manufacturing, supply chain management and logistics, preferably within renewable energy, solar, infrastructure or industrial sectors.
* Extensive experience managing large-scale manufacturing operations, including factory production, production planning, quality and operational efficiency.
* Strong experience in end-to-end supply chain, logistics and sales operations, including global sourcing, procurement, import/export, order management and customer fulfilment.
* Strong understanding of US trade regulations, import compliance, tariffs, customs procedures and logistics frameworks.
* Established relationships with government authorities, regulatory bodies, customs officials, port authorities and key industry stakeholders.
* Proven track record of building and managing large operational teams, vendor ecosystems and strategic partnerships, with strong commercial and cost management capabilities.

**Desired Qualifications**

* Experience in the solar, renewable energy or energy manufacturing ecosystem.
* Previous experience leading operations for a global manufacturing or industrial organisation.
* Experience managing manufacturing facilities and cross-border operations between the US and international markets, preferably India.
* Ability to build and scale operational infrastructure in a fast-growing business environment.

**Why ZetSol Energy**

* Opportunity to play a key leadership role in building ZetSol Energy's US operations.
* Work closely with the CEO and leadership team in shaping the company's operational strategy.
* Opportunity to build and scale a large operational and supply chain ecosystem.
* Be part of a growing solar manufacturing and supply chain platform backed by Zetwerk's global manufacturing capabilities.

Work Location: In person

records.title: Sr. Director -Engines Manufacturing
records.description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

You will lead Huntsville manufacturing for the BE-4 and Northstar engines—powerful engines that support Blue Origin’s launch vehicles and our mission to build a road to space. Reporting to the Vice President of Engines Manufacturing, you will lead senior managers and teams responsible for production, industrialization, and continuous improvement.

This hands-on leadership role balances the immediate need to deliver BE-4 engines with the work of bringing Northstar into production and scaling manufacturing capability for the future. You will partner across Blue Origin to deliver safely, reliably, on schedule, and at planned cost.

### **Responsibilities**

* Lead BE-4 and Northstar manufacturing in Huntsville, delivering to customer, program, safety, quality, schedule, and cost commitments.
* Sustain and improve BE-4 production while transitioning Northstar from development into stable, repeatable production.
* Develop production strategies, capacity plans, and operating rhythms aligned with program needs and company operating plans.
* Coordinate factory readiness, equipment identification and procurement, capital improvements, production start-up, and process qualification.
* Partner with Engineering, Program Management, Supply Chain, Test Operations, Quality, Safety, and other Blue Origin sites to resolve constraints and improve hardware flow.
* Lead improvement efforts across manufacturing, business processes, production planning, and resource utilization; apply lessons learned and standardize effective practices.
* Manage the manufacturing capital portfolio and ensure projects are executed safely and on schedule.
* Champion mission assurance and safety principles, including the planning and execution of critical operations.
* Develop leaders and teams, strengthen organizational capability, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Identify opportunities to improve safety, quality, cost, capacity, and delivery performance. 

### **Minimum qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in industrial, manufacturing, mechanical, or electrical engineering, or equivalent experience.
* 15+ years of experience in aerospace or a closely related complex manufacturing industry.
* Significant experience leading manufacturing or production organizations, including through senior leaders.
* Experience managing customer relationships and expectations.
* Experience with program- or project-level financial performance, budgets, or profit and loss.
* Proven ability to lead complex projects, coordinate across functions, and deliver in a fast-paced environment.
* Expertise in production operations, manufacturing process development, and continuous improvement.
* Strong understanding of quality systems, root cause analysis, and risk-based problem solving.
* Demonstrated commitment to safety, including experience planning and overseeing critical operations.
Strong communication, judgment, personnel management, and mentoring skills. 

### **Preferred qualifications**

* Master’s degree in engineering or a related field; MBA or equivalent business experience.
* Experience transitioning complex products from development into production and scaling manufacturing rates.
* Experience launching or expanding a production facility.
* Knowledge of fabrication, assembly, integration, test, quality, and configuration management.
* Experience managing facility-level capital improvements and equipment procurement.
* Lean Manufacturing, Toyota Production System, or Six Sigma experience; Black Belt certification is a plus.
Experience leading operations across multiple departments, programs, or sites. 

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. records.description:
**Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future**
======================================

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

**Why This Role Exists**
------------------------

Hadrian is building an additive manufacturing capability that runs as part of an autonomous factory, not as a room full of printers. The hard problem is not any single machine, material, or line of code. It is making all of them behave as one system. Systems engineering is the glue that holds that system together, and this role owns the glue.

The Senior Director leads three engineering functions, materials and process engineering, hardware engineering, and software engineering, and is accountable for the digital backbone that binds them to each other and to applications engineering: the architecture, interfaces, and data that connect Hadrian’s Opus platform to cutting-edge additive manufacturing equipment, add automation where it makes sense, fuse sensor data into the part record, and turn a collection of parts into a full, integrated digital manufacturing system built around additive.

The measure of success is not three strong teams. It is one manufacturing system that a customer part flows through, from design intent to qualified hardware, with every decision and every data point captured along the way.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* **Architect the system.** Define and control the end-to-end architecture for additive at Hadrian: requirements, interfaces, data model, and acceptance criteria that hold across multiple equipment platforms, modalities, and sites. Treat the factory as the product.
* **Build the digital backbone.** Connect additive equipment, peripherals, and inspection assets to Opus with the same discipline a semiconductor fab applies to connecting tools to the host: standardized state models, telemetry, event streams, and data contracts, with security and configuration control built in.
* **Fuse the sensors.** Bring in-situ monitoring, machine telemetry, environmental data, and downstream inspection into one correlated record per part, then move from monitoring to data-driven release and, where it is justified, closed-loop control.
* **Automate where it pays.** Lead automation across additive cells (material and powder handling, build changeover, part removal and depowdering, post-processing flow, robotics, controls, and safety) with a written case for each: safety, repeatability, and data capture first; labor second. Never automate an unstable process.
* **Lead the three functions as one.** Set standards, priorities, and cadence for materials and process, hardware, and software engineering. Resolve conflicts between them at the architecture level, not the escalation level.
* **Own the applications engineering interface.** With the Head of Applications Engineering, define what a production-ready hand-off looks like, publish the process capability and design-rule data applications engineers build to, and close the loop from floor results back into design guidance.
* **Industrialize the equipment.** Through the hardware engineering leader, own factory and site acceptance, commissioning, reliability (preventive maintenance, spares, MTBF/MTTR), and configuration-controlled modification and upgrade of additive systems, and lead the technical relationships with equipment partners that unlock deeper integration. The machine-level depth lives in that team; the standards and the outcomes live here.
* **Design for the factory.** Partner with Factory Development and Factory Automation on cell and site design: material flow, capacity, simulation, utilities, and the path to lights-out operation for additive.
* **Build quality in.** Make the system itself the evidence: traceability, data integrity, and process control that stand up to AS9100 audits and customer qualification without a separate paper trail.
* **Be the additive voice in Hadrian’s platform.** Carry additive requirements into Core Engineering and the Opus roadmap, and bring platform capability back to the floor.
* **Hire, develop, and retain.** Build a leadership bench under you, set a high technical bar, and make Hadrian the place the best additive systems engineers in the country want to work.

**What We’re Looking For**
--------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a physical science; an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
* 12+ years in advanced manufacturing, with real depth in at least three of these six domains: factory design and industrial automation; semiconductor or other high-reliability capital-equipment engineering; manufacturing software and data systems; materials science and process engineering; quality systems in regulated industries; sensing, process monitoring, and sensor fusion.
* 5+ years leading engineering teams, including leading through managers and building at least one function from the ground up.
* Production experience with metal laser powder bed fusion, as a user of the equipment, a developer of it, or both.
* Has led the integration of complex equipment into factory-level software (manufacturing execution, equipment host, or data platforms), including requirements, interface standards, and acceptance criteria.
* Has taken at least one production automation or capital-equipment program (robotic cells, material handling, or equipment with safety systems and controls) from concept through commissioning in a regulated environment (aerospace and defense, semiconductor, medical, or similar), and has owned the reliability of production equipment afterward.
* Fluent across the stack: can review a process flow, a data schema, a metallurgical cross-section, and a controls narrative in the same meeting, and knows which one is lying.
* Has worked as a true peer to a customer-facing or design function, with a record of building clean interfaces rather than absorbing the other team.
* Willing to travel up to 20%, including to Hadrian sites and international partners. Must meet the ITAR requirements below.

**What Will Set You Apart**
---------------------------

* Ph.D. in materials science, mechanical engineering, systems engineering or a related discipline.
* Semiconductor capital-equipment background: equipment-to-host integration, tool matching, fleet data, fault detection and statistical process control at scale.
* Equipment-maker experience developing or launching metal additive systems (new product introduction, cost-productivity trades, design reviews) in addition to user-side experience.
* In-situ monitoring and sensor fusion implemented in production, with data-driven release or closed-loop control.
* Factory design: material flow planning, discrete-event simulation, and highly automated or lights-out operations.
* AS9100 and customer qualification pathways; familiarity with AM specifications (ASTM F42, ISO/ASTM 529xx, SAE AMS 7xxx series).
* Budget or P&L ownership of a capital-intensive program, with a record of making the build-versus-buy and automate-versus-wait calls well.
* Modern software fluency: APIs, event streaming, OT/IT architecture, industrial interoperability standards (OPC UA, MTConnect), and cloud data platforms.

**Compensation**
----------------

For this role, the target salary range is $300,000 - $350,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

**Benefits for Full-time Employees**
------------------------------------

* Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees
 
 401k
* Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.
* Flexible vacation policy
* Equity

**ITAR Requirements**
---------------------

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

**Use of AI in hiring**
-----------------------

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy.

**Consideration of Criminal History**
-------------------------------------

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

**Hadrian Is An Equal Opportunity Employer**
--------------------------------------------

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

Compensation Range: $300K - $350K

records.title: Director, Operations Program Management
records.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 Agility Robotics is scaling its operations — and the programs that enable that scale need to be led with rigor, depth, and autonomy. As Director, Operations Program Management, you will own two things simultaneously: a team of technical and non-technical program managers working across all of the operations and supply chain domains and a portfolio of high-complexity programs that span the full organization. 

 Reporting to the Sr. Director of Operations Program Management & Insights, you will bring the structure, judgment, and leadership presence to operate with minimal oversight. You set the standard for what great program management looks like on this team. 

 This is the right role for someone who leads from the front, develops the people around them, and can drive complex cross-functional programs to outcomes without being told how to get there. 

 About the Work 

 
 Lead and develop a team of dedicated program managers. Set clear expectations, coach toward growth, and hold yourself accountable to building a stronger team over time. 

 Establish and model PM best practices across the team. You are both the standard-setter and the coach. 

 Own, through your and the team’s efforts, a portfolio of complex programs that require a high degree of structure, judgment, and organizational reach. Act as a player-coach on the team’s broader portfolio — holding your own programs while helping your direct reports navigate blockers and deliver against theirs. 

 Translate complex, multi-org work into clear progress narratives for executive audiences. You know what leadership needs to see and how to present it. 

 Identify risks, stalled decisions, and at-risk dependencies before they become problems.  

 Other duties as assigned. 

 
 About You 

 
 10+ years in leadership roles, with a proven track record in Program Management. 

 Exceptional ability to translate complex concepts into clear messages for diverse audiences. 

 Build and mentor a diverse and growing team of technical and non-technical Program Managers. 

 Strong data-driven decision-making skills to manage a complex portfolio of initiatives across a range of departments. 

 Operate with a high degree of autonomy defining the path for you and the team. 

 Deep understanding of how manufacturing and operations environments work — with 7+ years of experience driving programs in this space. 

 Comfort working in organizations without mature systems, clean data, or clear processes. 

 
 Bonus Points 

 
 Prior experience managing or developing a team of program managers. 

 Background in high-growth hardware, automation, or robotics environments. 

 Experience designing or overhauling operational processes at scale — service operations, order fulfillment, or manufacturing workflows. 

 
 
  

 Location 

 
 This is a hybrid position based out of our Salem office.

 
 The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Agility Robotics is a multi-state employer and this salary range may not reflect positions who work in other locations. These ranges may be modified in the future. 
 Anticipated Base Salary Range
 $149,000 — $193,000 USD 


 In addition to base pay, our competitive total rewards package consists of the following for full-time employees: 

 
 401(k) Plan:   Includes a 6% company match.

 Equity:   Company stock options.

 Insurance Coverage:   100% company-paid medical, dental, vision, and short/long-term disability insurance for employees.

 Benefit Start Date:   Eligible for benefits on your first day of employment.

 Well-Being Support:   Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

 Time Off: 
 
 Exempt Employees:   Flexible, unlimited PTO and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown.

 Non-Exempt Employees:   10 vacation days, paid sick leave, and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown, annually.

 


 On-Site Perks:   Catered lunches four times a week and a variety of healthy snacks and refreshments at our Salem and Pittsburgh locations.

 Parental Leave:   Generous paid parental leave programs.

 Work Environment:   A culture that supports flexible work arrangements.

 Growth Opportunities:   Professional development and tuition reimbursement programs.

 Relocation Assistance:   Provided for eligible roles.

 Annual Discretionary Bonus: Provided for eligible roles.

 
 All of our roles are U.S.-based. Applicants must have current authorization to work in the United States. 

 Agility Robotics is committed to a work environment in which all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. Each individual has the right to work in a professional atmosphere that promotes equal employment opportunities and prohibits unlawful discriminatory practices, including harassment. Therefore, it is the policy of Agility Robotics to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, national origin, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Agility Robotics prohibits any such discrimination or harassment. 

  

 Agility Robotics does not accept unsolicited referrals from third-party recruiting agencies.  We prioritize direct applicants and encourage all qualified candidates to apply directly through our careers page.  If you are represented by a third party, your application may not be considered.  To ensure full consideration, please apply directly.

records.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
records.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies. 

 Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.

 Purpose

 Guide the integration of cutting-edge manufacturing technologies into production, ensuring reliability, cost efficiency, and quality. This role shapes the future of Divergent’s manufacturing by enabling new processes, supporting high-mix hardware, and mentoring engineers to deliver industry-leading results.

 The Role

 
 Lead a multi-disciplinary team of manufacturing engineers responsible for driving design-for-manufacturing, process development, and implementation of advanced manufacturing methods across the DAPS manufacturing architecture.

 Oversee manufacturing requirements, process specifications, and root cause investigations to ensure reliable, high-quality production.

 Set team priorities, track projects, and mentor engineers to achieve critical company milestones.

 Develop industry-leading approaches to manufacturing process qualification, production scalability, and automation.

 Implement advanced manufacturing strategies in areas such as machining, additive manufacturing, assembly, bonding, coatings, and joining.

 Identify and deploy novel manufacturing technologies to improve quality, reduce cost, and increase throughput.

 Collaborate closely with design, materials, quality, and production teams to influence hardware design and production readiness.

 
  

 Basic Qualifications

 
 Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls 

 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, or a related discipline.

 3+ years of experience in a leadership role within manufacturing engineering.

 8+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering role, with significant exposure to aerospace or defense industries.

 Proficiency in CAD software (e.g., Siemens NX, AutoCAD) and strong understanding of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T).

 Experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems.

 Hands-on experience with advanced manufacturing techniques, including additive manufacturing, robotics, and automation.

 Proven track record of leading complex projects from concept through production, focusing on high-performance materials and high-reliability applications.

 
 Preferred Qualifications

 
 Master’s degree in a relevant engineering discipline.

 Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent expertise in continuous improvement methodologies.

 Familiarity with quality management systems like AS9100 or ISO 9001.

 Demonstrated ability to thrive in a high-tech, fast-paced startup environment with a passion for disrupting traditional manufacturing paradigms.

 
  

 Compensation

 
 Senior Manager / M07: $165,800 - $227,950

 
  

  
 Pay Range
 $142,900 — $227,950 USD 


 What We Offer Our Regular, Full-Time Employees: 

 
 Holistic Compensation Package: Enjoy a world-class compensation package that includes a competitive salary, equity plan, and discretionary results-based incentive bonus opportunities, ensuring you're truly valued for your contributions.

 Wellness and Time Off: Embrace a healthy lifestyle with paid vacation, sick time, and company holidays, including a year-end shutdown to recharge. We support growing families with paid parental leave, recognizing the importance of bonding time.

 Comprehensive Health and Wellness: Prioritize your well-being with our comprehensive health and wellness benefits, offering both HMO and Premium PPO options. Additionally, benefit from company-sponsored life insurance and short and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind.

 Investment in Growth: We're committed to your professional development. Take advantage of reimbursement opportunities for learning and development initiatives, empowering you to continuously expand your skill set and reach peak performance.

 Collaborative and High-Performing Environment: Join our collaborative, dynamic, and high-performing team within a fast-paced, mission-driven company. Together, we're disrupting the traditional manufacturing industry, fostering innovation, and integrating people and technology to reduce our footprint. 

 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
 Divergent is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected characteristic. Divergent provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act. 
 EEO Poster  

 In order to adjust to changes in our business, it may become necessary to add, remove or modify certain duties and responsibilities, or to reassign you to another job position. From time to time you may be asked to work on special projects or to assist with other work. Your cooperation and assistance in performing such additional work is expected.  
   
 E-Verify: Right to Work 
 Our company participates in E-Verify . E-Verify is a program that electronically confirms a candidate’s eligibility to work in the United States after completing the Employment Eligibility Verification (Form I-9). The information provided on the Form I-9 is compared to the records contained in the Social Security Administration and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) databases. This helps employers verify the identity and employment eligibility of newly hired employees. 
 Eligibility to Work Poster (English) |  Eligibility to Work Poster (Spanish) 
   
 Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance (FCIHO) 
 Pursuant to the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance (FCIHO), we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. 

 No agencies, no solicitations, and no calls please.
