records.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Bedrock's technology is scaling rapidly —over the next twelve months, we will rapidly scale our machine count, partners, and sites while also adding net-new machine types and a next-generation platform.  

The Head of Operations Planning & Special Projects owns aligning cross-functionally on an integrated machine plan across types, generations, product lines, partners, sites in order to develop Operational headcount and material plans; ultimately, giving the business a clear view of what's required and by when. 

You'll own the integrated machine plan, scenario planning, cross-functional alignment when constraints arise, building headcount scaling factors and plans, and standing up our early Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Reporting to the VP of Operations, you'll be a critical thought partner to the VP and each Operations Lead.


WHAT YOU'LL DO


INTEGRATED PLANNING

 - Own the integrated operations plan covering requirements across all product lines, machines, field headcount, and material readiness.

 - Identify constraints in the plan and build scenarios that drive resolution or acceptable alternatives.

 - Partner with each Operations leader to surface optimizations, risks, and constraints, and develop paths to mitigation.

 - Support senior leadership and board-level decisions with clear, rigorous analysis.

 - Partner with the VP of Operations to define team OKRs, the mechanisms to track them, and routine reporting on critical initiatives.

 - Contribute to the long-term forecast, integrating priorities across multiple teams.

 - Help align data collection needs with operational optimizations to strengthen our data pipelines.


S&OP PROCESS IMPLEMENTATION

 - Partner with Commercial, Finance, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Operations to build stage-appropriate S&OP processes that tee up critical business decisions, surface constraints, and evaluate alternatives.

 - Own the monthly S&OP cycle end to end: forecast development, demand review inputs, forecast analysis, supply plan integration, pre-meeting coordination, and reporting.

 - Forecast demand, assess whether projected supply can meet it, and define key performance metrics such as forecast accuracy and fulfillment rate.

 - Serve as the bridge between business strategy, engineering build plans, finance, and supply chain execution.


PRODUCTION PLANNING COORDINATION

 - Own phase-in / phase-out planning for new machine types, product lines, partners and sites, and hardware generations — including availability, supply constraints, retrofits, and partner transitions.

 - Track lead times and drive alignment on critical decision timelines and order dates.

 - Work with Operations leaders to plan labor availability, using key ratios and operational planning drivers.

 - Partner with Supply Chain and Contract Manufacturing to plan production capacity against demand, consolidate risks, and drive prioritization when supply is constrained.


OPERATIONS INSIGHTS & ANALYTICS

 - Own the development of core operational metrics and routine reporting.

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to the business.

 - Support continuous improvement across Operations through process and data.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - A single, trusted integrated plan that the business uses to make decisions about machines, people, and materials.

 - Constraints surfaced early, with clear scenarios and recommendations — not surprises.

 - A functioning monthly S&OP cadence with consistent participation and clear decisions.

 - Core operational metrics defined, tracked, and reviewed on a regular rhythm.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - 8–10 years in operations, planning, or program leadership, including 5+ years working with cross-functional teams distributed across sites or regions.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence leaders — aligning cross-functional stakeholders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth.

 - Track record implementing S&OP or supply-and-demand processes that bring clarity to requirements, decisions, and success criteria.

 - Experience planning and managing hourly / field workforce headcount.

 - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills; able to turn data into operational decisions.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including with executives.


PREFERRED

 - Familiarity with autonomy, heavy machinery, and/or the construction industry.

 - Experience standing up supply-and-demand review processes that clarify timelines, requirements, decisions, risks, and solutions.

 - Continuous improvement, Lean, or Six Sigma experience, including standing up an improvement program.


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

As Bedrock scales, the hardest problems are increasingly about coordination: getting the right machines, people, and parts to the right sites at the right time. This role builds the planning backbone that lets every Operations team — and the company — make faster, better decisions with confidence.

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.




ABOUT THIS ROLE



The Director, Commercial Operations will be the operational backbone of Crusoe's Energy Development Group. This person owns the analytical frameworks, pipeline processes, and team capabilities that allow Crusoe to evaluate and advance land and power opportunities at speed and at scale. From complex financial modeling and market analysis to pipeline integrity and board-level reporting, this role ensures the BD team operates with precision and strategic clarity.

This is a leadership-first, analytically grounded role. The ideal candidate brings deep experience in energy project finance or development, a track record of building and mentoring high-performing analyst teams, and the process orientation to continuously raise the quality bar on how Crusoe evaluates and advances opportunities. You will work closely with senior leadership across Energy Development, Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams and will be a key contributor to the operational health of Crusoe's project pipeline.




WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING ON

 - Overseeing the integrity and accuracy of Crusoe's data center opportunity pipeline, ensuring leadership has a reliable, real-time view of the project portfolio

 - Supervising the creation of board-level presentations, project approval materials, and executive communications that translate analytical complexity into clear strategic recommendations

 - Tracking and synthesizing hyperscaler activity, regulatory developments, and domestic energy infrastructure trends to surface actionable intelligence for the team

 - Supporting cross-functional collaboration between Energy Development and the Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams to move projects efficiently through the development pipeline

 - Guide the team in leveraging internal data analytics tools and external market intelligence to identify and vet opportunities

Own pipeline management and process improvement

 - Drive continuous improvement of business operations processes within the Energy Development team, including project management, due diligence workflows, and reporting mechanisms

 - Develop and implement best practices for tracking key pipeline metrics and project statuses

Deliver executive-ready reporting and communications

 - Supervise the creation and delivery of board-level presentations, project approval materials, and ad hoc reports for senior management

Support cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder engagement

 - Support the team in communications with external stakeholders including developers, IPPs, and potential partners

Monitor market and regulatory intelligence

 - Oversee tracking and analysis of hyperscaler and co-located data center activity, regulatory changes in the energy sector, and domestic energy infrastructure investments

 - Ensure the team synthesizes this information to identify potential impacts and opportunities for Crusoe




QUALIFICATIONS

Required

Preferred

records.description:

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About This Role:

Our Senior QMS Manager, Manufacturing is responsible for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continuously improving Crusoe's Quality Management System (QMS) across all manufacturing and operational facilities. Owning the enterprise QMS framework, this role ensures quality processes, controls, records, procedures, and compliance activities are effectively executed and scaled across the organization.

Reporting into our Director of Quality, the QMS Manager partners closely with Product Quality, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and EHS to transition the organization from site-specific, paper-focused processes to a data-driven, risk-based, and preventive Quality Operating System. From leading internal and external audits to governing CAPA/NCR workflows, document control, and new site QMS launches, this role is pivotal in building an agile quality system that enables rapid business growth.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

 - QMS Framework & Governance: Own and maintain the overall Quality Management System. Establish QMS policies, standards, and governance mechanisms that bridge operational gaps and scale with manufacturing expansion.

 - Standards & Regulatory Compliance: Maintain organizational compliance with ISO 9001, customer standards, and applicable regulatory requirements. Monitor evolving standards and translate compliance requirements into practical operational controls.

 - Audit Program Leadership: Direct the enterprise audit program—including internal, customer, supplier, certification, and regulatory audits. Oversee audit planning, execution, finding closure, and transition the company toward a proactive quality culture.

 - CAPA & NCR Governance: Own enterprise nonconformance (NCR) and Corrective/Preventive Action (CAPA) processes. Standardize root-cause analysis (RCA), containment, and effectiveness verification while tracking systemic trends to prevent issue recurrence.

 - Document & Change Control: Manage the Quality Document Management System and change-control governance. Ensure current procedures, specs, and records are accessible at points of use and prevent the use of obsolete documentation.

 - Quality Records & Systems Integration: Establish quality record data governance. Partner with IT/Business Systems to integrate QMS data across ERP, MES, and inspection tools to drive enterprise-wide quality visibility.

 - Quality Metrics & Management Reviews: Establish cross-site quality dashboards tracking NCR/CAPA aging, audit findings, COPQ, and training compliance. Lead periodic Quality Management Reviews with executive leadership to convert quality data into strategic decisions.

 - Training & Quality Culture: Define role-based QMS training requirements, maintain competency records, and deploy quality awareness initiatives that foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

 - Continuous Improvement & Process Maturity: Eliminate non-value-added quality steps, lead Lean Six Sigma projects, and establish closed-loop feedback between operational performance and QMS enhancements.

 - Enterprise Quality Risk Management: Institute risk-based QMS governance. Maintain quality risk registers and ensure high-risk processes receive appropriate controls, audits, and management oversight.

 - New Site Expansion: Lead QMS readiness activities for greenfield manufacturing sites, ensuring required procedures, forms, training, and controls are operational prior to production launch.

 - Cross-Functional Partnership: Serve as the primary QMS subject-matter expert, partnering with Product Quality, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Engineering, and Supply Chain to drive systemic issue resolution.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - Educational Foundation: Bachelor's degree in Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Operations, or a related field.

 - Professional Experience: 7+ years of experience in Quality, QMS, Quality Engineering, or Manufacturing Quality, with demonstrated success developing and scaling QMS frameworks.

 - Quality Standards Expertise: Deep working knowledge of ISO 9001 standards, quality management principles, and regulatory compliance.

 - Audit Management: Proven track record of planning, executing, and managing internal, customer, regulatory, and third-party certification audits.

 - Root Cause & CAPA Mastery: Strong expertise in CAPA, NCR, 8D, 5-Why, Fishbone, and structured problem-solving methodologies.

 - Document & Change Control Governance: Demonstrated experience managing quality document control systems, record retention, and engineering/operational change management processes.

 - Cross-Functional Leadership: Strong ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive accountability without relying solely on direct authority.

 - Analytical & Communication Skills: Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills with the ability to translate complex quality data into actionable business strategies.

 

Bonus Points:

 - Professional Certifications: ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE).

 - Process Excellence: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.

 - ISO Implementation: Direct experience leading ISO 9001 implementation, recertification, or multi-site expansion.

 - Systems & Digital Transformation: Experience implementing enterprise QMS software platforms (e.g., MasterControl, ETQ, Veeva) and integrating QMS with ERP/MES systems.

 - Scaling Environment: Experience establishing QMS frameworks within fast-growing manufacturing organizations or greenfield facility launches.

 - Advanced Quality Technologies: Experience leveraging AI, predictive analytics, or digital transformation tools in quality management.

 

Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation:

records.title: Vice President of Operations
records.description:
Quindar builds software to manage satellites like servers. We are seeking a Vice President of Operations to build the operating system, organizational infrastructure, and business processes that turn company strategy into execution as we scale across commercial and government markets.

This leader owns business operations, strategy and performance, facilities, and General & Administrative functions. Beyond running the operating cadence, the role connects corporate strategy, resource allocation, and cross-functional execution so that Quindar consistently makes the right investments and turns them into business outcomes. The role holds the authority to resolve cross-functional prioritization conflicts at the leadership level, with clear and intentional escalation to the CEO, while functional leaders retain accountability for their results and authority over their teams.

Facilities, Business Operations, and the G&A team report to this role, with their leaders responsible for day-to-day execution. This is a hands-on executive role for someone who can build a function, develop its leaders, and drive execution across the company.



Company Execution and Performance Management

• Translate company strategy into company OKRs and functional commitments with accountable owners, deadlines, dependencies, and approved resources.

• Agree with each functional leader on a small set of meaningful KPIs with clear definitions, source data, targets, and reporting frequency, and maintain a consolidated performance dashboard across Sales, Product, Engineering, Programs, Finance, People and Brand, and Operations.

• Design and run the company operating model: quarterly planning, leadership reviews, decision tracking, and follow-up, with a visible record of commitments delivered, missed, corrected, and rescoped.

• Design and implement a company-wide model for cross-functional prioritization and decision-making at the leadership level, including decision rights and escalation paths, aligned with and actively reinforced by the CEO.

• Use the operating data to drive decisions and corrective actions, resolve cross-functional dependencies, and escalate decisions that put company goals at risk.

• Partner with functional leaders and the VP of Finance to align workforce capacity, hiring plans, facilities, and budgets with company priorities.



Corporate Strategy and Go-to-Market

• Help shape corporate strategy with the CEO and leadership team, including evaluating markets and opportunities, defining investment requirements, and translating strategic choices into resourced plans.

• Lead the cross-functional planning and execution of GTM priorities in partnership with the CEO, who leads Sales & Marketing: align Product, Engineering, Programs, and Operations behind revenue priorities and ensure the organization is resourced to deliver them.

• Lead the evaluation and incubation of new business opportunities, including, but not limited to,Operations as a Service (OaaS). For OaaS, lead the initial cross-functional effort to take the offering from concept toward launch, including the business model, service definition and commercial terms, investment requirements, and operational readiness.

• Ensure new services, markets, and programs are integrated into company planning, performance management, and compliance from the outset.



AI-Enabled Business Operations

• Lead the AI Business Operations team to build and deploy workflows that reduce manual coordination and increase output across Quindar, with measurable reductions in hands-on processing time and sustained adoption.

• Identify and baseline the highest-value workflows across functions, prioritizing those that remove coordination overhead between Product, Engineering, Programs, Sales, and Marketing (for example, specifications to engineering tickets, user documentation, marketing materials, and proposal development).

• Build internal knowledge infrastructure, such as a company data warehouse of product knowledge, engineering designs, documentation, and marketing and proposal content, that any role can query or use to create collateral through an agentic interface.

• Implement appropriate access controls, source traceability, and compliance requirements, including CUI handling, before any workflow handling sensitive or consequential outputs enters production use.



Facilities and Classified Readiness

• Own facilities planning, buildouts, workplace operations, vendor management, and procurement across all unclassified and classified spaces.

• Maintain an integrated master schedule covering construction, procurement, vendors, budget, and readiness for each space, with a defined risk and impact scale, reviewed regularly with the CEO.

• Deliver the facilities infrastructure needed for classified readiness, completing facilities work ahead of accreditation target dates and obtaining Security’s written acceptance against an agreed readiness checklist.

• Partner with Security, IT, Contracts, and program leadership so that facilities, policies, training, and records support classified program and audit requirements. Security retains accreditation responsibility.



General and Administrative Operations

• Lead legal operations, and corporate administrative services through internal teams and outside partners.

• Manage outside counsel and coordinate corporate legal matters, employment matters, contract review, and company policies.

• Own cap table and stock option administration in partnership with Finance and legal counsel, and maintain corporate records and board and stockholder approval workflows with the CEO and counsel.

• Own the administrative infrastructure required to pursue and support government business, including SAM.gov http://SAM.gov registration, applicable NSTXL and consortium memberships, JCP certification/DD Form 2345, and a centralized calendar of registrations, renewals, and reporting obligations.

• Oversee export compliance program administration, including applicable ITAR/EAR processes, working with qualified counsel and designated compliance personnel.

• Coordinate corporate insurance, business continuity planning, corporate overhead efficiency, and company-wide operational risk management.



Fundraising and Finance Partnership

• Lead operational, legal, people, and corporate diligence readiness for fundraising alongside the VP of Finance, including an organized data room and timely, accurate responses to investor requests.

• Support board materials and investor reporting with company operating metrics, organizational plans, and progress against strategic priorities.

• Partner with Finance on operating plans, overhead budgets, and the investments needed to support the next stage of growth and new business lines.



Qualifications

• Experience leading operations at a growing technology company, with exposure to government contracting or another regulated market.

• Demonstrated success building teams, systems, and operating processes through a significant stage of organizational growth.

• Experience contributing to corporate strategy and leading cross-functional GTM or new-business initiatives from concept to launch, with a bias toward revenue and business outcomes.

• Experience across facilities, legal operations, compliance, or business operations.

• A hands-on track record of using AI, technology, and automation to improve operational efficiency.

• Familiarity with venture-backed company governance, equity administration, and fundraising diligence.

• Ability to turn ambiguous priorities into clear plans, coordinate executive peers, and hold teams accountable for commitments.

• Strong judgment about when to act directly, delegate, escalate, or engage specialist expertise.



What Success Looks Like

• Company strategy is reflected in OKRs, KPIs, and commitments with clear owners, and leaders run the business from a trusted, shared dashboard.

• Cross-functional prioritization decisions are made quickly and consistently at the leadership level, with less day-to-day intervention from the CEO.

• GTM priorities and new services such as OaaS move from strategy to resourced, cross-functionally executed plans with measurable revenue impact.

• AI-enabled workflows are in production across functions, materially reducing manual coordination while meeting access-control and compliance requirements.

• Facilities for classified operations are delivered on schedule and accepted by Security.

• Organizational structures, career frameworks, equity programs, and scaling processes are ready ahead of growth to 150+ employees.

• Required registrations, compliance obligations, and corporate and equity records remain current and diligence-ready.



Security Clearance Eligibility Requirement
Due to U.S. Government contractual requirements, this position requires eligibility for a U.S. Government security clearance. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance; therefore, candidates for this position must be U.S. citizens. An active clearance is not required at the time of hire but is preferred and may be required in the future based on program needs.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

 - To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/ddtc_public/ddtc_public?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.


WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING AT QUINDAR

 - We work in a cutting edge industry and you will get the opportunity to be part of a small team with a large direct impact on the success of our customers’ space missions!

 - We take work life balance very seriously. We require employees to take 15 days off but provide unlimited PTO and follow most US federal government holidays.

 - Mental health is just as important as physical so we provide quarterly health & wellness benefits.

 - Comprehensive health insurance for you and your family with 100% coverage for employees.

 - We encourage employees to save for retirement and provide 4% 401(k) matching.

 - Each quarter we have a 4-day company offsite. Previous locations include San Francisco, Nashville, Denver, Santa Fe, New Orleans, San Diego, Bozeman, and New York City.

 - Our culture and company is evolving. You will be key in creating the next major or minor version!

records.title: Commissioning Chief Engineer, Marauder
records.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.



Commissioning Chief Engineer, Marauder

Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing defense autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

Job Summary:

In this role you will be responsible for the commissioning and operation of the engine room and all associated machinery aboard a novel autonomous vessel. You will ensure that all marine systems — including but not limited to main propulsion, auxiliary machinery, fuel oil, lubrication, cooling, and associated environmental equipment — are properly tested and validated through structured commissioning processes and integrated with the vessel's autonomy and software control systems to support reliable manned, remote, and autonomous operation.

The ideal candidate will possess strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities, along with the ability to develop procedures and processes in support of a novel commissioning environment. Have a strong grasp on vessel engineering systems with the ability to work independently on issues, including drafting and refining operational and technical documentation where none previously existed. A steadfast commitment to safety and adherence to maritime regulations is essential for ensuring the highest standards in vessel operations.

Responsibilities

 - Lead and support commissioning activities for autonomous vessels, including system testing, validation, and troubleshooting prior to and during operation.

 - Collaborate with autonomy and software engineering teams to verify integration between traditional machinery control systems and the vessel's autonomy stack across manned, remote, and autonomous operating modes

 - Develop, write, and refine standard operating procedures, checklists, and technical documentation from scratch in the absence of established processes

 - Complete all necessary maintenance on vessel machinery.

 - Always be on-call while on-hitch to address any issues that arise.

 - Manage inventory and ordering of spare parts.

 - Assist in the shipboard execution of mission objectives.

 - Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with team members, stakeholders, and senior management.

 - Problem-solving abilities and a proactive approach to addressing challenges.

 - Strong leadership skills to lead a team in a dynamic environment and pitch in when your skills are applicable while working across teams.

 - Travel to multiple locations while on hitch

Required Qualifications

 - Valid U.S. Coast Guard MMC

 - National Chief Engineer of Motor, Unlimited Horsepower Endorsement.

 - STCW Endorsements of Chief Engineer, OICEW, Basic Training, Advanced Firefighting

 - Valid USCG STCW Medical Certificate

 - Valid TWIC, USCG STCW Medical Certificate, and Passport.

 - Proficiency in maritime engineering systems, particularly electrical systems

 - Ability to work both independently and as a part of a group

 - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams

 - Pass background check and USCG/DOT drug testing prior to onboarding.

 - Security clearance and eligibility required

 - Projected 28/28 schedule

Desired Qualifications

 - Familiar with jet-drive marine engines

 - Experience with autonomous or unmanned systems

 - Experience with software engineering

 - Experience with automation systems.

Physical Demands

 - Ability to certify as “fit for work” by demonstrating ability to swim and tread water

 - Frequently and repetitively, lift, push and carry up to 50 lbs.

 - Will be exposed to marine environments, including sun, wind, rain, cold, and saltwater spray, often for extended periods

 - Must be able to operate in daylight, low-light, and night conditions using marine navigation systems and visual cues

 - Ability to perform physically demanding work i.e. stoop, lay, bend, reach, squat, kneel, crouch, twist and crawl for extended periods of time including up to 12 hours/day

 - Climb and maintain balance on ladders, platforms, or other high structures

 - Ability to stand and walk for up to 10 hours a day, including over varied and uneven terrain

 - Climb and maintain balance on ladders, scaffolding or other high structures

 - Ability to work in a hot and humid environment and follow safe practices to stay hydrated

 - Hearing ability sufficient to detect alarms, verbal instructions, and workplace hazards in a high-noise environment.

 - Must be able to work in a shipyard environment, including indoor fabrication shops, onboard vessels under construction, and outdoor areas exposed to changing weather conditions.

 - Wear Personal Protective Equipment, including but not limited to: safety glasses, safety shoes, hard hat and adhering to prescribed safety rules and guidelines

Benefits

 - Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

 - Saronic pays 99% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

 - Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

 - Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

 - Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan

 - Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

 - Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

 - Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

If this role is based in the United States, it requires access to export-controlled information or items that require “U.S. Person” status. As defined by U.S. law, individuals who are any one of the following are considered to be a “U.S. Person”: (1) U.S. citizens, (2) legal permanent residents (a.k.a. green card holders), and (3) certain protected classes of asylees and refugees, as defined in 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/8/1324b.

Saronic does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities and benefits. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

records.title: Staff Quality Engineer
records.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




POSITION OVERVIEW

The Staff Quality Engineer serves as the VP of Quality's senior technical quality expert responsible for driving multi-site RCCA culture, supporting engineering and manufacturing quality. Reporting directly to the VP of Quality, this role leads enterprise-wide technical investigations, drives engineering-based Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA), and partners across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Product, and Mission Operations to improve product reliability and operational performance.

This position applies deep engineering expertise to identify fundamental technical failure mechanisms, validate corrective actions through engineering analysis and testing, and eliminate systemic product and process risks.

The Staff Quality Engineer operates across multiple manufacturing sites and product lines, working with cross functional teams on design opportunities, manufacturing processes, and operational readiness while establishing best practices for technical problem solving across the enterprise.




TECHNICAL PROBLEM SOLVING

 - Apply structured engineering methodologies to determine true physical, process, software, or systems root causes—not simply procedural gaps.

 - Utilize advanced analytical tools including Fault Tree Analysis, Fishbone, 5 Why, Statistical Analysis, Tolerance Stack Analysis, and FMEA.

 - Validate corrective actions using engineering data, experimentation, testing, and verification.

 - Drive permanent corrective actions that eliminate recurrence across products and manufacturing sites.




MULTI-SITE QUALITY LEADERSHIP

 - Provide technical quality leadership across multiple manufacturing locations.

 - Standardize RCCA methodologies and engineering investigations across the enterprise.

 - Coach site Quality Engineers on advanced engineering problem solving.

 - Lead enterprise technical reviews for recurring issues and customer escapes.

 - Support rapid problem escalation and recovery during production interruptions.




ROOT CAUSE & CORRECTIVE ACTION (RCCA)

 - Lead enterprise RCCA for manufacturing defects, supplier escapes, customer returns, field failures, and reliability issues.

 - Ensure investigations identify technical root causes rather than symptoms.




MANUFACTURING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT

 - Improve manufacturing capability through engineering analysis.

 - Reduce defects through process optimization rather than increased inspection.

 - Support New Product Introduction (NPI) Quality activities across multiple product lines.




CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Program Management, Product Management, Mission Operations, and Executive Leadership.

 - Present technical findings and recommendations to cross functional teams.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical or aerospace engineering.

 - 10+ years of engineering aerospace, defense, automotive, or advanced manufacturing.

 - Demonstrated success solving complex engineering problems.

 - Extensive experience leading engineering-based RCCA.

 - Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations.

 - Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.

 - Must be able to travel 30-50% of the time.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Design and development engineering management experience




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Establish an enterprise technical RCCA methodology across all manufacturing sites.

 - Reduce quality escapes through permanent corrective actions.

 - Improve manufacturing FPY.

 - Mentor Quality Engineers in advanced engineering problem solving.




BENEFITS

 - Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium under the basic plan for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

 - Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

 - Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

 - Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan with company match

 - Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

 - Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

 - Pet Insurance: Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline

 - Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

 

Saronic CCPA Notice for Candidates and California Employees https://saronic-assets-public.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Saronic%20CCPA%20Notice%20for%20Candidates%20and%20California%20Employees.pdf



If this role is based in the United States, it requires access to export-controlled information or items that require “U.S. Person” status. As defined by U.S. law, individuals who are any one of the following are considered to be a “U.S. Person”: (1) U.S. citizens, (2) legal permanent residents (a.k.a. green card holders), and (3) certain protected classes of asylees and refugees, as defined in 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/8/1324b.

Saronic does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities and benefits. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

records.title: Head of Supply Chain & Manufacturing Strategy

postedPay.title: Head of Supply Chain & Manufacturing Strategy

records.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Skydio is committed to becoming a world class manufacturing company. U.S. policy is moving toward secure, domestic drone supply chains and evolving policy on component origin, supplier eligibility, market access and import duties are raising the bar for every manufacturer in the industry. Skydio has historically been at the forefront of investing in US manufacturing and blue supply, and we are doubling down on our commitments to ensure America leads the next frontier of flight. This role will drive the strategic plan to build the drone manufacturing mecca and the stable and compliant supply chains that feed it.




BUILDING ON A HEAD START

Skydio is the largest U.S.-based drone manufacturer, and we have treated secure supply chains as a strategic investment from the start. All of our current drone solutions, including X10, Dock for X10 and R10, are on the Blue UAS Cleared List. We have outgrown four U.S. manufacturing facilities in eight years. In April 2026 we committed $3.5 billion over five years to expand U.S. manufacturing through our SkyForge initiative, R&D and supply chain development. That includes a new U.S. factory five times the size of our current space and directing more than $1 billion to domestic suppliers. Through SkyForge, select suppliers will co-locate production with Skydio and work alongside our engineers, expanding and in some cases starting domestic manufacturing of critical parts. You will spearhead the SkyForge initiative and help decide where that investment goes and make sure it pays off: which components to onshore first, which suppliers to develop, and which capabilities to bring in-house.

Skydio is committed to becoming a world class manufacturing company. U.S. policy is moving toward secure, domestic drone supply chains and evolving policy on component origin, supplier eligibility, market access and import duties are raising the bar for every manufacturer in the industry. Skydio has historically been at the forefront of investing in US manufacturing and blue supply, and we are doubling down on our commitments to ensure America leads the next frontier of flight . This role will drive the strategic plan to build the drone manufacturing mecca and the stable and compliant supply chains that feed it.




WHAT YOU'LL NAVIGATE

 - NDAA restrictions and the American Security Drone Act

 - The Blue UAS Cleared List and Blue UAS Framework

 - The DDP Supply Chain Framework and its phased component requirements

 - The FCC Covered List and equipment authorization

 - Section 232 tariffs and country-of-origin requirements




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Regulatory Partner: You will work closely with our regulatory team to understand current regulations, policy direction and will work directly with key partners setting this policy to help influence

 - Supply Chain and Manufacturing Strategy: Determine which capabilities and technologies we onshore, vertically integrate or partner on to build robust and compliant supply chains

 - Onshoring and supplier development: Set priorities for securing and onshoring supply across our critical commodities with the commodity teams. Where a domestic or allied supply base does not yet exist, decide whether to develop a supplier (including through SkyForge), bring the work in-house, or design around the constraint.

 - Make-versus-buy and vertical integration: Assess which production we should bring into our U.S. facilities and build the case with Manufacturing, Supply Chain and Finance. A well-supported recommendation against integration is as valuable as one for it.

 - Product compliance risk: Maintain a live, evidence-backed view of where each product line stands against each regulation. Translate it into schedule, revenue and cost terms the leadership team can act on, and report on a regular cadence.

 - Supplier-of-record decisions during design: Work alongside Global Supply Managers (GSMs) and hardware engineering during NPI to set SPOR. Bring the regulatory screen into design reviews early enough that engineering can still act on it.

 - Multi-tier traceability: Stand up bill-of-materials traceability to tier three and beyond, with country of origin and chain of custody, across purchased and in-house components.

 - Compliance and cost together: Find moves that serve compliance, tariff and domestic-content goals at once, and look for other opportunities to drive domestic sourcing to cost parity with traditional supply chains.
 
 


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

90 days: A complete risk baseline across products and regulations, separating hard blockers from cost problems, with named owners for every gap and a first readout to leadership.

3 months: An approved sourcing and supplier-development plan, a first vertical integration recommendation, and compliance screening built into design reviews. Each product line has a decided market-access pathway.

6 months: No launch is surprised by a compliance gap. Onshoring and supplier investments are prioritized by where they build the most durable advantage, and make-versus-buy decisions weigh compliance, tariff and domestic-content effects together.



WHAT YOU BRING


REQUIRED

 - 10+ years in supply chain, manufacturing operations, commodity management or operations strategy, including at least 3 in a regulated hardware environment where sourcing decisions carried legal or contractual consequences.

 - Experience influencing component and supplier selection during design, through NPI, design reviews, or SPOR and approved vendor list (AVL) decisions.

 - Credibility with both a sourcing organization and a factory. You can discuss capacity, tooling and yield as fluently as supplier qualification.

 - Accountable ownership of a multi-tier country-of-origin, supplier compliance or trade compliance program.

 - A make-versus-buy or vertical integration analysis you personally built and defended, including capex and ramp assumptions.

 - A track record of turning technical findings into executive decisions, and of changing engineering or sourcing decisions you had no formal authority over.

 - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.


PREFERRED

 - Working knowledge of NDAA §889/§848, country-of-origin and substantial-transformation analysis, Buy American domestic-content tests, or DFARS and FAR flow-downs

 - Background in in-house manufacturing, UAS, aerospace and defense, defense electronics, or EMS and contract manufacturing

 - Commodity experience in batteries and cells, motors and magnetics, imaging or thermal sensors, or PCB and PCBA

 - Experience standing up a production line or bringing an outsourced process in-house

 - Experience with a Blue UAS or Green UAS submission, or a DCMA or DCSA assessment

 - Experience developing domestic or allied-country suppliers from scratch




HOW THE ROLE FITS

 - Reports to: Head of Hardware Operations. Individual contributor at hire, with a path to building a small team as the program grows.

 - Peers: VP of Supply Chain and VP of Manufacturing.

 - Partners: Regulatory, Manufacturing Engineering, GSMs, Program Leads, Trade Compliance and Finance.

 - Visibility: Regular briefings to the leadership team on SkyForge progress. Several decisions this role informs are capital-allocation decisions.

Compensation: At Skydio, our compensation packages for regular, full-time employees include competitive base salaries, equity in the form of stock options, and comprehensive benefits packages. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual base salary range for this position is $229,500 - $302,500*. Fundamentally, we believe that equity is the key to long-term financial growth, and we ensure all regular, full-time employees have the opportunity to significantly benefit from the company's success. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. This position and all associated benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as the Company’s policies and eligibility criteria.

*Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position’s location.

records.title: Director, Product Quality
records.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 We are looking for a hands-on, high-impact Director, Product Quality  to lead our Field Quality and Failure Analysis engineering teams. In this role, you will hold ultimate accountability for overall field quality, reliability performance, and fleet health across all deployed commercial products. 

 You are a seasoned practitioner of rigorous problem-solving methodologies (8D, 5-Why, DMAIC) with a proven track record of diving deep into complex electromechanical, hardware, and firmware failures. You will bridge the gap between field service operations, customer sites, supplier quality, and internal product design teams to ensure field issues are contained rapidly, root-caused definitively, and prevented permanently. 

 About the Work 

 
 Own Field Quality & Fleet Health: Establish, monitor, and report on key field quality metrics (e.g., MTBI, MTTF, ARR, issue escape rates, service ticket turnaround time) for all shipping products and customer deployments. 

 Lead Failure Analysis (FA) & CAPA: Lead and grow a dedicated team of Failure Analysis Engineers. Drive rigorous Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Corrective/Preventive Action (CAPA) processes for field returns, hardware bugs, and system-level failures. 

 Field Containment & Rapid Response: Establish immediate containment protocols for critical field escalations, safety events, and unexpected fleet-wide failure trends to minimize customer downtime. 

 Cross-Functional Feedback Loop: Serve as the critical bridge between Field Operations, Customer Success, Hardware Engineering, Software/Firmware, and Supplier Quality. Drive design-for-reliability (DFR) feedback directly into next-generation product engineering. 

 Manage Closed-Loop Quality Systems: Implement and maintain robust Closed-Loop Corrective Action (CAPA) tracking across multi-site field deployments and repair depots. 

 Executive Communication & Governance: Host regular Field Quality Reviews with leadership, presenting objective data, failure Pareto analyses, root-cause findings, and measurable CAPA progress. 

 
 About You 

 
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. 

 Experience: 10+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Field Quality, or Reliability Engineering within high-complexity hardware industries (Robotics, Automotive/EV, Aerospace, Autonomous Systems, or Complex Industrial Equipment). 

 Leadership: 5+ years of direct people management experience leading technical engineering teams (FA, Quality, or Sustaining Engineering). 

 Hands-on Expertise: Deep, practical experience executing physical failure analysis on electromechanical systems (actuators, harnesses, sensors, PCBAs, battery management systems, and precision mechanical linkages). 

 Methodologies: Certified or expert practitioner in structured root cause analysis tools (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa, Fault Tree Analysis, FMEA, Gauge R&R). 

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Advanced Degree: Master’s degree in Engineering Management or an Engineering discipline. 

 Certifications: Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE), or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt. 

 Domain Experience: Experience managing field reliability for autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), humanoid robotics, or safety-critical industrial equipment. 

 Systems Exposure: Familiarity firmware diagnostic tools, and telemetry data analytics for remote fleet diagnostics. 

 
 Work Environment & Travel 

 
 Position is based out of our Salem, OR facility with regular access to testing labs, service centers, and assembly lines. 

 Occasional travel (up to 20%) to customer sites, field test locations, or primary suppliers may be required to investigate critical quality escapes. 

 
 
 Location 

 
 This is an onsite position at our Salem, OR office. 

 
 The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Agility Robotics is a multi-state employer and this salary range may not reflect positions who work in other locations. These ranges may be modified in the future. 
 Anticipated Base Salary Range
 $162,000 — $210,000 USD 


 In addition to base pay, our competitive total rewards package consists of the following for full-time employees: 

 
 401(k) Plan:   Includes a 6% company match.

 Equity:   Company stock options.

 Insurance Coverage:   100% company-paid medical, dental, vision, and short/long-term disability insurance for employees.

 Benefit Start Date:   Eligible for benefits on your first day of employment.

 Well-Being Support:   Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

 Time Off: 
 
 Exempt Employees:   Flexible, unlimited PTO and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown.

 Non-Exempt Employees:   10 vacation days, paid sick leave, and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown, annually.

 


 On-Site Perks:   Catered lunches four times a week and a variety of healthy snacks and refreshments at our Salem and Pittsburgh locations.

 Parental Leave:   Generous paid parental leave programs.

 Work Environment:   A culture that supports flexible work arrangements.

 Growth Opportunities:   Professional development and tuition reimbursement programs.

 Relocation Assistance:   Provided for eligible roles.

 Annual Discretionary Bonus: Provided for eligible roles.

 
 All of our roles are U.S.-based. Applicants must have current authorization to work in the United States. 

 Agility Robotics is committed to a work environment in which all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. Each individual has the right to work in a professional atmosphere that promotes equal employment opportunities and prohibits unlawful discriminatory practices, including harassment. Therefore, it is the policy of Agility Robotics to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, national origin, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Agility Robotics prohibits any such discrimination or harassment. 

  

 Agility Robotics does not accept unsolicited referrals from third-party recruiting agencies.  We prioritize direct applicants and encourage all qualified candidates to apply directly through our careers page.  If you are represented by a third party, your application may not be considered.  To ensure full consideration, please apply directly.

records.title: Director, Workplace Operations
records.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

 OUR MISSION 

 True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

 OUR VALUES 

 
 Be the offset.   We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

 What would it take?  We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

 It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

 
 BENEFITS & PERKS *

 
 Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options

 Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave

 Fuel for your day: Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees

 And more: 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays

 Equity participation: Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

 
 *Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

 YOUR MISSION 

 We are looking for an operations leader to take ownership of the everyday workplace operations at True Anomaly. From office management to culinary, janitorial to groundskeeping to beyond, you'll lead the teams and vendors that keep our workplaces running at a high standard. You own the full OPEX picture for our workplaces — managing to budget, forecasting with rigor, and always bringing cost-saving options to the table. You think in partnerships: working hand-in-hand with Real Estate to draw the line between Landlord scope and ours and with Development Planners to set long-term standards that drive operational efficiency downstream. You're a people leader at heart, a sharp cross-functional partner, and you'll flex to support services in our production areas when the mission calls for it. You take immense pride in your craft, and that pride shows up everywhere — in workplaces that run well, employees who feel taken care of, and an operations function that scales like a well-oiled machine.

 RESPONSIBILITIES 

 Lead and develop operations teams across multiple workplaces to support ongoing day-to-day needs, including office management, culinary/snacks, janitorial, groundskeeping, and related services. Define and own third-party vendor strategy across all service categories, ensuring consistent quality, reliability, and cost-effectiveness across the portfolio. Own the full OPEX budget for our workplaces, reporting out on forecast vs. budget regularly and surfacing cost-saving options. records.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

 OUR MISSION 

 True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

 OUR VALUES 

 
 Be the offset.   We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

 What would it take?  We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

 It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

 
 BENEFITS & PERKS *

 
 Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options

 Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave

 Fuel for your day: Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees

 And more: 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays

 Equity participation: Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

 
 *Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

 YOUR MISSION: 

 At True Anomaly, production is a strategic advantage. Our ability to rapidly build, integrate, test, and deliver high-performance systems at scale is critical to mission success and long-term competitiveness.

 As Vice President of Production, you will build our production organization into a high-rate, quality focused build and test machine.  You will drive vertical integration to achieve pace and cost targets while developing automation and test infrastructure to support lights out verification across multiple product lines and mission sets. You will own manufacturing, assembly/integration, EGSE design and production, quality, and test and test automation — building the operational systems, infrastructure, and teams required to scale efficiently without compromising quality or speed.

 This role is responsible for creating a data-driven production organization that continuously improves throughput, reliability, and cost while enabling rapid iteration and delivery across the business.

 Key Responsibilities 

 
 Lead all manufacturing, assembly, integration, and production test operations across the company’s product lines while supporting prototyping for research and development.

 Develop and execute the production strategy required to scale from development programs into repeatable, high-rate manufacturing.

 Own the operational execution of the company’s vertical integration efforts, including standing up internal manufacturing and test capabilities for propulsion systems, fluid systems, PCBAs, FlatSats, RF systems, and integrated space vehicles.

 Build scalable production systems, workflows, and operational infrastructure that improve throughput, quality, and delivery performance across complex hardware production environments.

 Drive implementation of lean manufacturing principles, automation, and data-driven operational management across production environments supporting spacecraft, missile defense, and mission-critical component and payload systems.

 Own development and deployment of production tooling, EGSE, fixtures, and automated test systems required to support scalable manufacturing, integration, and environmental test operations.

 Partner closely with Engineering teams to drive design-for-manufacturing and design-for-test principles into product development.

 Establish production metrics, dashboards, and operational review processes focused on cycle time, yield, labor efficiency, throughput, and cost reduction.

 Lead quality execution across manufacturing, integration, inspection, RF test, propulsion test, and production verification activities, ensuring quality is embedded into operational processes.

 Drive automation of test execution, production data collection, and operational reporting to improve repeatability, traceability, and decision-making.

 Collaborate with Supply Chain, Engineering, Facilities, Security, and Program Management to ensure aligned production readiness and execution across both classified and unclassified production environments.

 Build and mentor high-performing teams capable of supporting rapid company growth and operational scale.

 Support long-term facility, staffing, secure manufacturing, and production capacity planning to meet future mission demand.

 
 Required Qualifications 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or related technical field

 15+ years of experience leading manufacturing, production, integration, or operations organizations in complex technical industries

 Proven experience scaling production operations from development into repeatable manufacturing environments

 Strong background in manufacturing, assembly/integration, production test, and operational execution for complex electromechanical or aerospace systems

 Experience standing up vertically integrated manufacturing or test capabilities across areas such as propulsion systems, fluid systems, PCBAs, RF systems, or integrated vehicle production

 Demonstrated success driving operational excellence, quality improvement, and cost reduction initiatives

 Experience implementing data-driven manufacturing systems, KPIs, and production management processes

 Strong understanding of design-for-manufacturing, production scaling, environmental test, and test automation principles

 Experience operating within high-complexity manufacturing environments

 Proven ability to lead large multidisciplinary teams in fast-paced, highly technical environments

 Excellent cross-functional leadership and communication skills

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Experience in aerospace, defense, launch vehicle, missile defense, or high-rate hardware manufacturing environments

 Familiarity with propulsion manufacturing and test operations, including additive manufacturing / 3D printing processes

 Experience with spacecraft integration and environmental test campaigns

 Familiarity with classified manufacturing and secure production operations

 Experience supporting rapid production scaling across multiple product lines

 Background implementing lean manufacturing or continuous improvement frameworks at scale

 Experience with automated manufacturing, MES, or production data systems

 Experience building operational organizations during periods of rapid company growth

 
 Compensation   

 
 Base Salary: $300,000 - $350,000 

 
 
 Equity + Benefits  including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO, and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave   

 
 Additional Requirements   

 
 Work Location – We observe an in-person work environment, and expect 4 days per week in office at the Company's Denver, CO headquarters or at our facility in Long Beach, California. 

 
 
 Security Clearance – Ability to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI clearance required. 

 
 This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below. 

  
 To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

 True Anomaly is committed to equal employment opportunity on any basis protected by applicable state and federal laws. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.

 To protect candidates and our company from application fraud and impersonation, we use third-party tools to verify applicant identity and detect fraudulent applications. Learn more in our Privacy Notice .

records.title: Head of Bedrock Operations Center
records.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Head of Bedrock Operations Center (BOC) to build and lead the central, always-on hub that oversees our deployed autonomous machines. As the Bedrock System deployments scale across new states, new machine types, and a next-generation platform, the BOC is how we keep every machine safe, productive, and supported around the clock.

This role owns three core functions: Remote Assistance, supporting autonomous machines in real time when they need a human decision; Customer & Partner Support, the single front door for customers, partners, and field teams; and Central Operations, which provides live visibility, dispatch coordination, and incident coordination and command.

The Head of BOC owns the Operations Center's operating model, organization, tooling requirements, performance, and manpower oversight. The BOC is accountable for the safe remote operations, uptime, and responsiveness our customers experience. Reporting to the VP of Operations, this leader is a critical thought partner to Product and to Operations Leads across the company.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Operations Center Strategy & Build-out

 - Define the BOC operating model, org structure, and coverage model (shifts, time zones, follow-the-sun) as the fleet scales

 - Build and lead the BOC leadership team and a growing workforce of shift leads and specialists

 - Own workforce planning and ensure adequate, qualified staffing; Partner with Product and Engineering on machines-per-operator ratios against fleet growth, product mix, and new machine types

 - Own the physical and technical readiness of the Operations Center, including infrastructure, redundancy, connectivity, and business continuity

Remote Assistance

 - Own round-the-clock remote operations for autonomous machines, including response-time SLAs, escalation protocols, and clear decision authority

 - Establish safety-first standards for remote interventions, remote stops, and hand-offs to on-site personnel, in partnership with Safety teams

 - Build training, certification, and quality-assurance programs for remote assistance operators

 - Analyze intervention data and partner with Autonomy Engineering to reduce interventions and improve machine autonomy over time

Customer & Partner Support

 - Build and lead a tiered support function (L1 / L2 / L3) with clear escalation paths into Field Operations, Service, Hardware, RA, and/ or Engineering

 - Define and deliver support SLAs tailored to each product line and customer commitment

 - Own ticketing, knowledge base, and customer communication standards; turn voice-of-customer trends into fixes

 - Partner with the Commercial team on customer onboarding, service commitments, and account health

Central Operations / Command & Control

 - Own live, fleet-wide situational awareness: machine status, health, location, and utilization across every site

 - Coordinate daily dispatch, service, and maintenance with Field Operations, including parts and technician routing

 - Serve as incident command for operational and safety events, with clear playbooks for triage, escalation, communication, and post-incident review

 - Own runbooks, shift hand-off standards, and change management for new sites, new machine types, and new platforms

Performance & Analytics

 - Define and track core BOC metrics: intervention rate and response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, fleet uptime, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to leadership

 - Lead continuous improvement through process, automation, and data, increasing the number of machines each operator can safely support


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Autonomous machines get fast, safe human support whenever they need it

 - Customers and partners have one clear front door and consistently fast resolution

 - Real-time visibility into every machine and site, with incidents handled calmly and transparently

 - Machines-per-operator rises steadily as intervention insights drive autonomy improvements

 - The Operations Center scales ahead of fleet growth, new sites, and new machine types without a drop in service

Required

 - 12+ years in operations leadership, including 5+ years building and leading 24/7 or mission-critical operations (command centers, remote operations, network or fleet operations, or large-scale support organizations)

 - Experience building an operations organization from early stage to scale, including hiring and developing managers and shift leads and managing large hourly and/or contract workforces

 - Track record defining and managing SLAs, escalation paths, and incident response in safety-critical or high-availability environments

 - Experience influencing engineering, product, and commercial leaders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth

 - Strong analytical skills; comfortable with operational data, dashboards, and forecasting models (SQL / BI tools a plus)

 - Experience with workforce planning, scheduling, and shift-based operations

 - Excellent written and verbal communication with customers, field crews, and executives

Preferred

 - Experience running operations centers for autonomous vehicles, robotics, trucking, aviation, or mining

 - Experience leading remote assistance, teleoperation, or fleet response teams for autonomous systems

 - Familiarity with heavy machinery and/or the construction industry

 - Experience building B2B or technical support for industrial equipment or hardware products

 - Familiarity with fleet telemetry, monitoring and alerting, ticketing, and workforce-management tools

 - Experience launching operations across multiple regions or time zones

 - Continuous improvement / Lean / Six Sigma experience
