records.description:
**Director of Manufacturing (Rubber)**

The Director of Manufacturing will oversee rubber production operations across 2 manufacturing plants with 200 total employees, 100 employees per plant, 1 union plant & 1 non-union, 5-8 Direct Reports (Department Managers) with responsibility for safety, quality, delivery, and cost, acting as leader with accountability for both operations.

**Location**
: Columbia, Missouri (Relocation Assistance Offered)

**Compensation**
: $175,000 - $215,000 base salary + 15% bonus.

**Benefits**
: Medical, Dental, Vision, STD, LTD, 401k Match 6%, 3 weeks PTO, Tuition Assistance, etc.

**Job Description:**

*Operational Leadership & Plant Management*

* Hold full P&L, safety, quality, delivery, and cost accountability for both rubber manufacturing plants across textile & milling operations including mixing and cord production, acting as a multi-site operations leader.
* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team of 6-8 managers who in turn lead roughly 200 salaried and hourly employees across multiple shifts.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, capital plans, and budgets; manage conversion cost, yield, scrap, rework, material variance, and overhead against targets.
* Balance production schedules and capacity across both sites to meet downstream Belt and Hose demand, optimizing changeovers, inventory, and material availability.
* Partner with the VP of Manufacturing, plant managers of downstream operations, supply chain, and commercial teams on demand planning, capacity strategy, and make-versus-buy decisions.
* Spend meaningful time on the floor at each site (approximately 30% travel), maintaining a visible presence on all shifts and engaging directly with operators and supervisors.

*Compound Quality, Technology & Process Control*

* Own end-to-end compound consistency, using rheology (Mooney, MDR/RPA), physical properties, and downstream processing and molding results as the measures of success.
* Reduce process variation through structured methods such as design of experiments (DOE), statistical process control, capability studies, and root cause analysis.
* Develop, standardize, and improve mixing programs (load order, ram pressure, rotor speed, mix time, dump temperature, energy-based and multi-stage mixing) for new and existing compounds, including EPDM, CR, HNBR, NBR, SBR, and NR systems.
* Oversee textile operations (cord unwinding, coating, and rewinding) and raw material handling, heating, and cooling to ensure consistent adhesion and reinforcement performance in finished belts and hoses.
* Lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, the materials lab, process and manufacturing engineers, and downstream operations, leading investigations through disciplined experimentation.
* Establish a single, controlled system of work instructions, batch cards, and process parameters across both sites so that the same compound is produced the same way regardless of site, shift, or operator.
* Evaluate and recommend mixing equipment, automation, weighing/batching, and tooling options for current and new processes and products.

Mill: raw materials are received and handled, then weighed, mixed, heated, and cooled to produce uniform rubber compound for downstream product production.

Textiles: cord is carefully unwound, coated, and rewound to specification, giving finished products consistent strength and adhesion.

*Safety, Compliance & Culture*

* Champion a zero-harm safety culture, including lockout/tagout, machine guarding, mill nip and pinch-point hazards, hot surfaces, combustible dust, and chemical handling.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, environmental permitting, SDS requirements, and applicable customer, ISO/IATF, and corporate standards.
* Drive 5S, standardized work, and lean manufacturing practices; treat housekeeping as both a safety and a quality requirement.
* Build a culture of accountability in which following the documented process is the standard and deviations are surfaced openly.

*Talent Development & Organizational Capability*

* Build a bench of operators, leads, supervisors, and managers through structured training, skills matrices, cross-training, and succession planning.
* Set clear expectations, conduct performance reviews, and partner with HR on coaching, corrective action, recognition, and labor relations.
* Capture experienced operators' tribal knowledge and convert it to documented, teachable standards.
* Attract, hire, and retain top technical and operational talent in a competitive labor market.

*Strategy & Continuous Improvement*

* Work with the plant leadership and engineering leadership to define annual improvement initiatives, then align cross-functional teams to targets and track results.
* Lead capital projects, technology transfers, and new-process launches from concept through ramp-up.
* Use KPIs, trend charts, and daily management routines to drive visibility, problem solving, and sustained results.
* Contribute to the North American and global compounding strategy, sharing best practices with sister sites and corporate technology teams.

*Key Performance Indicators*

* Safety: recordable incident rate, near-miss reporting, and audit results
* Compound first-pass quality and out-of-spec rate; rheology capability and variation reduction
* Downstream molding and processing results attributable to compound and cord
* Schedule attainment and on-time delivery to downstream operations
* Scrap, rework, yield, and material and conversion cost versus budget
* Equipment uptime and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)
* Operator qualification coverage and cross-training depth
* Employee engagement, turnover, and leadership bench strength

**Qualifications Seeking:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Chemical, Polymer, Mechanical, Materials, or Industrial), Chemistry, or a related technical field preferred. Experience in lieu of Bachelors will be considered.
* 8+ years of manufacturing experience, including 5–10 years of hands-on polymer or rubber compounding and mixing experience.
* 5+ years of progressive leadership experience managing managers and multi-shift operations, including responsibility for safety, quality, cost, and delivery.
* Strong working knowledge of internal mixers (tangential and intermeshing), two-roll mills, TSE, weigh-up/batching, and compound testing (Mooney, MDR/RPA, specific gravity, dispersion).
* Demonstrated experience reducing process variation using DOE, SPC, and structured problem-solving methods.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, lab, engineering, and production teams.
* Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, direct without being abrasive.
* Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30% between sites and to work on the floor in a manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications (Not Required):**

* Master's degree in Polymer Science, Chemistry, or Engineering, or an MBA.
* Experience in belt, hose, or other engineered rubber product manufacturing, with understanding of rheology and downstream extrusion, calendering, and molding.
* Experience with cord treatment, textile reinforcement, or adhesive systems.
* Experience managing multi-site operations and leading change across sites.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification, or equivalent.
* Familiarity with ERP/MES systems, mixing control software, and automation for production and material traceability.
* Experience leading capital projects, new-equipment commissioning, or greenfield/expansion launches.

**Core Competencies Seeking:**

* Technical depth: credible expert in rubber chemistry, rheology, and mixing who can coach engineers and operators alike.
* Leadership: develops managers, builds accountability, and engages a unionized or non-union frontline workforce.
* Systems thinking: standardizes work and builds sustainable processes rather than relying on individual heroics.
* Analytical rigor: makes decisions with data, experimentation, and clear trend visibility.
* Business acumen: manages cost, capital, and capacity with a P&L mindset.
* Learning agility: quickly learns new technologies and applies them to business needs.

records.title: Director of Production
records.description:
**About the Opportunity**

A well-established manufacturing organization in the aviation and aerospace industry is seeking an experienced
**Director of Production**
to oversee and improve its manufacturing operations.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for someone with direct aerospace or aviation manufacturing experience who can manage production activities, lead teams, improve operational efficiency, and ensure consistent product quality and on-time delivery.

The ideal candidate is a practical, floor-oriented leader who understands production planning, manufacturing processes, equipment maintenance, and resource management.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Oversee daily manufacturing and production activities to ensure operational efficiency, product quality, and timely delivery.
* Manage production schedules, workflow, resource allocation, and manufacturing capacity.
* Lead and coordinate production planning and maintenance teams to maintain equipment reliability and operational continuity.
* Monitor production costs, operating expenses, and departmental budgets while identifying cost-saving opportunities.
* Establish and track KPIs related to productivity, production volume, quality, scrap rates, lead times, and on-time delivery.
* Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing processes, reduce waste, and increase production capacity.
* Ensure compliance with aviation manufacturing standards, safety regulations, environmental requirements, and customer specifications.
* Work closely with department managers and supervisors to establish performance goals and maintain accountability.
* Coach, develop, and mentor production leaders and supervisors.
* Support facility improvements, equipment upgrades, capital projects, and the implementation of new manufacturing technologies.
* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, teamwork, safety, and operational excellence.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field; equivalent experience will also be considered.
* Approximately 8–10 years of progressive leadership experience in a manufacturing environment.
* Direct experience in
 **aviation or aerospace manufacturing operations is required**
 .
* Previous experience managing production teams, manufacturing schedules, and operational resources.
* Strong understanding of production planning, manufacturing processes, maintenance coordination, and quality control.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated ability to improve productivity, control costs, and meet production targets.
* Strong leadership, problem-solving, organizational, and decision-making skills.
* **Fluency in both English and Spanish (written and spoken) is required.**

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience working with ERP systems; Quantum experience is a plus.
* Six Sigma Green Belt certification or higher.
* Lean Manufacturing or other continuous improvement certifications.
* Experience managing manufacturing budgets and operational performance metrics.

**Ideal Candidate**

The successful candidate will be a hands-on production leader who is comfortable working directly with manufacturing teams and supervisors. This position is best suited for someone with a strong background in aerospace manufacturing who can balance people leadership with daily production execution and continuous improvement.

records.title: OEM Manufacturing Director
records.description:
**Job Description**
As the Fort Wayne OEM Director of Manufacturing, you will be a key leadership contributor to the success of the Fort Wayne Manufacturing Hub. Reporting to the Hub Director of Manufacturing, you will provide inspirational leadership in a rapidly growing business and have responsibility for all original equipment manufacturing at the site. This role demands a strategic, results-oriented leader with a proven track record of building and scaling rapidly growing organizations. Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. This means work will be conducted on location at a BAE Systems facility 100% of the time.
 
 
 
 
**Key Responsibilities Include**
**Strategic Product Stream Leadership**

* Own the strategic direction, execution, and performance of the Circuit Card Assembly and Unit Integration factories
* Serve as the primary point of contact between production and program management

**Program Execution**

* Oversee execution of manufacturing in alignment with program schedules
* Ensure all contractual obligations (cost, schedule, performance) are met or exceeded

**Performance Improvement**

* Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma Principles
* Implement metrics to monitor production performance
* Initiate corrective actions to resolve production variances, quality escapes, and manufacturing cost variances

**Required Education, Experience, & Skills**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, Operations Management, or related field; equivalent experience considered OR 20 years manufacturing experience with no degree
* Minimum 10 years’ experience in production/manufacturing
* Minimum 6 years’ experience leading production/manufacturing teams including managing people leaders
* Proficiency with manufacturing management concepts
* Proficiency applying Lean Manufacturing principles and visual management tools

**Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills**

* Proficiency with Oracle ERP
* Formal Lean or Six Sigma training/certification
* Minimum 10 years’ experience leading people leaders of production/manufacturing teams

**Pay Information**
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743
 
 
Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.
 
 
Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.
 
 
 
 
**About BAE Systems, Inc.**
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.
 
 
Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.
 
 
This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled, or a qualified pool of candidates is identified.

Executive Manufacturing Leadership Opportunity
 
 
BASX is seeking a transformational manufacturing executive to lead one of its key operations as Site Leader (Director of Manufacturing).
 
 
This role is far more than manufacturing oversight. It is an opportunity to shape the future of a growing operation, influence enterprise strategy, drive large-scale operational transformation, and build the manufacturing capabilities required to support long-term business growth.
 
 
As the senior manufacturing leader for the site, you will serve as a trusted business partner to executive leadership and will be responsible for aligning manufacturing strategy, operational performance, capital investment, workforce development, and technology advancement with the organization's strategic objectives.

records.title: Plant Manager I
records.description:
This position leads all plant operations for a70+ employee, 2 shift, manufacturing site. This leader ensures day-to-day operations are delivered with the aligned objectives of safety-first mindset, customer satisfaction along with growing and developing the leaders within the facility. This position also plays a critical role in developing and executing capital project plans for the facility to enable continuous improvement and growth in market share.

This full-time position reports directly to region General Manager and is located at Liberty Packaging’s manufacturing plant in Houston, Texas

**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Directly lead and supervise a team of direct reports to deliver major site functions across manufacturing, shipping, maintenance, and scheduling.
* Own end-to-end performance for the facility to meet KPIs in the areas of Safety, Quality, Cost, and Delivery. Establish, measure, and monitor performance across facility and root cause performance issues. Develop and deploy plans to drive improvements in manufacturing processes to ensure superior product quality, reduced cycle times, lead times, and minimize overall manufacturing costs.
* Provide day-to-day leadership for manufacturing team decision-making in the areas of production, labor, material costs, design, and production scheduling.
* In partnership with Continuous Improvement function, guide leaders and front-line staff through the identification and deployment of continuous improvement initiatives with an impact on key performance indicators.
* Ensure the right talent and capabilities are in place to meet strategic objectives; accountable for establishing goals, managing performance, and developing teams to ensure short- and long-range objectives are achieved
* Establish a two-way communication & engagement culture to ensure all plant employees are clear on plant performance and connection to business performance, including KPIs.
* Lead key change initiatives across the plant in partnership with regional and functional support systems (e.g., continuous improvement, engineering, human resources, sales, etc.)
* Lead the successful identification, business case design, and execution of capital projects in partnership with functional teams and executive leadership. Ensure multi-year capital plans support market growth and customer delivery
* Ensure employee relations stay connected with open and continuous dialogue
* Develop and grow community engagement presence by representing plant locally in key activities and through execution of frequent employee and community engagement activities
* Own direct P&L responsibility for plant site
* Provide leadership by connecting and being visible to all three shifts daily
* Other duties, as assigned

**Required Education, Experience And Skills**

* Bachelors’ degree and 7+ years manufacturing experience OR 10+ years manufacturing industry experience in lieu of education
* 5+ years people leadership experience
* Experience analyzing downtime, production, and financial variance trends, and identifying actions to deliver expected performance
* Previous experience developing and managing a budget, forecasting, and monitoring results
* Experience with identifying and executing capital projects to drive improvement against KPIs
* Demonstrated experience with organizational effectiveness, operations management, and a proven track record of achieving results
* Experience developing and presenting information to multiple levels of the organization from front-line to executive leadership
* Superior time management, attention to detail, verbal and written communication skills, decision-making, and organization skills
* Excellent computer skills required, including Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
* Demonstrated entrepreneurial spirit

**Preferred Education, Experience And Skills**

* Previous experience with Amtech / CTI or Kiwi
* Previous experience with ERP systems
* Previous experience in corrugated or paper manufacturing
* Lean and / or Continuous Improvement certifications
* Bilingual English / Spanish

**Compensation & Benefits**

The starting base salary range for this position is $110,078 - $137,598 per year plus eligibility in annual bonus program. The compensation posted is the anticipated pay for the position at the time of the posting. We may pay above or below posted amount based on several factors, including, but not limited to education and/or certifications, skills, experience, or work location. Some positions may qualify for additional compensation in the form of bonuses or deferred compensation options.

At LDI, we are pleased to provide employees with a comprehensive benefits package including health/dental/vision insurance options; paid time off; 10 paid holidays; 401(k) plus company matching and annual discretionary profit sharing; flexible spending and health savings account options; life and disability insurance; tuition assistance; wellness and mental health resources, and financial advising services. Eligibility in benefit programs is based on hours worked per week.

**Physical Requirements**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* Regular sitting, standing, and walking throughout the day to accomplish tasks
* Manual and finger dexterity used regularly with some repetitive finger motions
* Ability to work in front of a computer screen for long periods of time
* Specific vision abilities include close and distance vision; able to identify colors, small letters, and numbers; hand/eye coordination, depth perception and able to adjust focus
* Hearing and speaking
* Other conditions may include frequent reaching, stretching, pushing, pulling, pinching, grasping, and gripping.

**About Our Company**

Comprised of multiple companies with headquarters in New Hope, Minnesota, Liberty Diversified International (LDI) is a privately held company employing more than 1,900 individuals across our manufacturing facilities, production facilities and core business operations in Minnesota, Iowa, Nebraska, Illinois, Mississippi, Texas, Arizona, Virginia, California, and Mexico. With deep roots in the corrugated box manufacturing industry, we operate in the core markets of paper, packaging, workplace products, corrugated plastics and building products.

Since 1918, our values – Caring, Innovation, Trust and Excellence – have guided our day-to-day activities. We believe that when our employees are aligned with these values, we create superior service and solutions for our customers. The LDI family of companies includes Liberty Packaging, Liberty Paper, Liberty Plastics (Custom Solutions and Quarrix Building Products) and Safco.

Liberty Diversified International is an equal opportunity employer and makes all employment decisions without regard to race, color, sex, religion, age, creed, sexual orientation, national origin, marital status, disability, or any other protected class.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

records.title: Sr. Manager Operations
records.description:
**Job Description**
**Description & Requirements**
**About AESC US LLC**
AESC is a global leader in the development and manufacturing of high-performance batteries for zero-emission electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Founded in Japan in 2007 and headquartered in Yokohama, AESC has been building manufacturing capabilities around the world in the U.S., U.K., Europe, Japan and China to serve key markets and leading customers locally for over 14 years. Today, AESC has become the partner of choice for the world's leading OEMs and energy storage providers in North America, Europe, and Asia. Its advanced technology powers over one million electric vehicles and provides more than 15GWh of installed capacity for battery energy systems in over 60 countries.
 
 
AESC is expanding its footprint in the United States, and the Blythewood Repack Operation supports the broader South Carolina production network. AESC is committed to our local communities where it is making its investments, creating jobs, and supporting local charities.
 
 
**About The Role**
The Senior Operations Manager provides comprehensive leadership of manufacturing operations, driving safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective production. This role is responsible for integrating production execution with workforce planning, material flow, equipment availability, quality performance, and operational readiness.
 
 
The successful candidate must possess a broad understanding of plant operations and demonstrate the ability to lead across functions rather than operate solely as a production manager.
 
 
****What You Will Do****

* Direct daily manufacturing operations across assigned shifts and production areas.
* Establish and execute production plans that align labor, equipment, materials, and customer delivery requirements.
* Manage operational KPIs including throughput, OEE, labor productivity, downtime, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery.
* Collaborate with Maintenance and Engineering to ensure equipment availability, preventive maintenance execution, and effective downtime response.
* Partner with Quality to manage manufacturing defects, process compliance, containment, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate with Supply Chain and Logistics to maintain effective material flow, inventory accuracy, and production readiness.
* Lead production supervisors and team leaders, establishing clear expectations for attendance, timekeeping, staffing, overtime controls, and employee performance.
* Manage operating expenses, labor utilization, and production resource requirements.
* Promote a disciplined safety culture with EHS and enforce manufacturing operating standards.
* Support commissioning, production ramp-up, process stabilization, and future plant expansion.
* Develop staffing, succession, and workforce capability plans.
* Complete other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**
****What You Need****

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline, or equivalent substantial manufacturing leadership experience.
* At least 10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including five years in plant operations leadership.
* Demonstrated accountability for manufacturing performance, staffing, safety, cost, and cross-functional execution.
* Experience with ERP/MES systems, Lean manufacturing, and operational performance management.

****What is "Nice to Have"?****

* Automotive OEM or Tier 1 experience.
* Battery manufacturing experience.
* High-volume automated manufacturing experience.
* Plant launch or greenfield ramp-up experience.

****Travel Requirements****
20% International Travel
 
 
****What We Offer****
Welcome to AESC, where you'll have the opportunity to tackle the world's most fascinating challenges alongside exceptionally talented individuals who are driven to make a difference. We strive to ensure that our employees are well taken care of, enabling them to focus on their work and contribute to our collective mission.
 
 
**We Offer**

* Comprehensive compensation packages including a competitive salary and a rewarding bonus program.
* An inclusive and diverse work environment that fosters and encourages professional and personal development.
* Highly automated, clean, safe, and temperature-controlled production environment.
* Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance.
* HSA and Flexible Spending Accounts.
* 401K with company match.
* Life Insurance (Company paid and additional voluntary life available).
* Paid Vacation and 14 Paid Holidays.
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage (Company Paid).
* Tuition reimbursement.

****Equal Employment Opportunity****
At AESC, we are committed to providing Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) to all individuals. We participate in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. Join us in our passion to design, manufacture, and sell high-performance products, contributing to a sustainable and zero-carbon emission future.
 
 
****Physical Requirements****
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable otherwise qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.
 
 

* Ability to stand, walk, and work on a concrete production floor for extended periods of time.
* Ability to read, write, speak, hear; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach and lift with hands and arms frequently throughout the day.
* Ability to wear all required PPE when working on the production floor.
* Required to occasionally lift, push, pull and/or move up to 10 pounds, and occasionally required to lift, push, pull and/or move up to 35 pounds.

****Work Environment****
The work environment is primarily a semi-automated/automated plant with a concrete floor and is characterized as climate controlled, moderate noise, and forklift traffic. The individual must be able to perform all essential functions as appropriate on the plant floor, in meetings, and with employees, management, customers and suppliers.
 
 
Candidate must perform the essential duties and responsibilities with or without reasonable accommodation efficiently and accurately, and without causing significant safety threat to self or others. The statements made herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this job classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive and inclusive list of all responsibilities, duties, and/or skills required of personnel so classified.
 
 
Hiring is contingent upon successful completion of a drug screen and background check, and verification of the candidate's eligibility to work in the United States. AESC US LLC is a drug-free workplace.

records.title: Sr. Manager, Optimus Operations
records.description:
**What To Expect**
The Senior Manager, Optimus Operations sets the vision and strategic path for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering within a major shop at Tesla’s new Optimus Factory in Austin, Texas. Openings span operations leadership across multiple shops—including Plastics, Machining, Actuators, and Assembly. Each role leads their shop teams and cross-functional partners to achieve Safety, People, Quality, Production/Delivery, and Cost KPI targets.
 
 
This role is responsible for production and resource planning; coaching, mentoring, and developing leaders; launching new Optimus manufacturing processes and programs successfully; and daily tactical planning and execution to achieve the build plan and meet safety, quality, rate, and cost targets. The person in this role must guide the team through complex issues, distill large volumes of data to solve problems, and drive day-over-day continuous improvement in a high-volume, high-precision factory environment.
 
 
This Senior Manager provides hands-on support, leadership, and direction on all operational, team morale, and equipment-related matters. The person in this role builds teams that work cohesively and perform at the highest level—keeping Tesla’s mission and the goals of the Optimus program in mind—while partnering closely with peer shop leaders and factory leadership across the Austin Optimus Factory.
 
 
**What You'll Do**- Set the vision and strategic path for Production and Maintenance in an assigned Optimus shop and lead the team to Safety, People, Quality, Production, and Cost KPI targets
- Drive tactical planning to hit the production build plan with the highest safety, quality, and yield, including identifying bottlenecks and addressing availability, efficiency, and yield constraints
- Launch new Optimus programs and lead production ramps and product/process design changes through resource planning, program management, and partnership with NPI, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain
- Guide the team through root cause analysis, first-principles thinking, and data-driven problem solving while maintaining standardized work and quality/safety compliance
- Coach, mentor, and develop Production, Maintenance, and Engineering leaders, instill process standardization and training, and drive continuous improvement
- Lead the maintenance organization on equipment availability, preventive and predictive maintenance, spare parts strategy, and uptime improvements for shop-critical assets
- Build a high-performing team with clear goals and feedback, improve morale with HR, and collaborate with peer shop Senior Managers to share best practices
**What You'll Bring**- Degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Materials, or Industrial Engineering preferred, or equivalent experience
- 7–10 years of leadership and manufacturing experience, preferably in automotive, robotics, plastics, precision machining, electromechanical assembly/actuators, general assembly, or another highly technical manufacturing environment
- Analytical, detail-oriented, self-driven critical thinker who communicates proactively and works well in a fast-paced, multicultural factory environment
- Experience with process-improvement methodologies, DOE/statistical methods, lean and world-class manufacturing practices, and standing up or ramping new factories, shops, or production lines
- Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to work under pressure, juggle competing priorities, and meet tight deadlines
- Ability to use structured problem-solving methods such as 8D, fishbone diagrams, and 5-Why analysis to resolve production problems
- High-level leadership and decision-making skills with a strong sense of urgency in a greenfield/new-factory ramp, plus proficiency in MS Office, Visio, CAD, SPC, data-analysis tools, Jira, Tableau/BI dashboards, and project-management tools
**Benefits**
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
 
- Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
- Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
- Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
- Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
- Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
- 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
- Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
- Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
- Employee Assistance Program
- Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
- Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
- Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
- Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
- Tesla Babies program
- Commuter benefits
- Employee discounts and perks program
- Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)
, Tesla

records.title: Sr Manager of Manufacturing Engineering
records.description:
**Company And Opportunity Overview**

WNA’s vision is to be a leading entrepreneurial player in terms of market share, agility, and game-changing solutions. WNA is a solution provider, creating value along the supply chain of our customers, from online purchase to their customers.

WNA is headquartered in the Charlotte Metro Area, North Carolina. With around 500 employees and ~$200M of sales, WNA focuses on the retail and distribution market segments with marquee customers such as Walmart, Amazon, and the majority of large grocers and retailers.

In addition to being the largest manufacturer of shopping carts in North America, WNA has three additional main product segments as well as a Service business, providing turnkey solutions for customer guidance (Access Systems), Shelving & Fixtures, and Material Handling products.

Access Solutions provides sophisticated customer guidance and loss prevention systems for major retailers. With German-engineered products and a strong installed base, this segment focuses on protecting existing market share while expanding into adjacent opportunities in smart retail, autonomous store technology, and digital integration.

Additionally, WNA offers a range of digital solutions integrated into our products, including advanced shopping cart containment systems, smart exit gate technology, and innovations for autonomous and semi-autonomous retail stores. We are continuously expanding and enhancing our digital offerings to meet evolving customer needs and drive industry advancement.

WNA is part of the Wanzl Group, headquartered in Germany, and has 12 plants in 8 countries, providing comprehensive, solutions-driven service and expert knowledge of local markets for customers across the globe through their 360° service.

**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Manage a team of 5-10 Engineers, CAD Designers, & Engineering Technicians
* Drive LEAN implementation / LEAN transformation.
* Recommend and manage capital projects from concept through appropriation process, to project management and implementation for current production improvement.
* Select, develop, and train the Manufacturing Engineering Team
* Provide needed technical support and lead shop floor problem solving using world-class problem-solving methodologies.
* Create and maintain shop floor layouts, fostering material flow optimization.
* Creating and maintaining Manufacturing BOMs and Routings in ERP system
* Support Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) driven by R&D
* Support Industrialization in developing & implementing new production methods/processes.
* Process Capability Studies
* Standard Work Analysis, for both Direct and Indirect Labor
* Create test protocols, document and track results.
* Support for Operations, support for Tooling and Maintenance, Look for Efficiency Projects to increase Capacity, OEE, Reduce costs (Labor, Material, OH, etc.) and drive projects in consequence, review PMs, Cycle Times analysis, Downtime analysis.
* Develop Set-up technicians.

**Skills And Experience**

* BS in Engineering from an accredited university
* Minimum of 5 years engineering experience in a Manufacturing Environment, Design/R&D, & demonstrated engineering project leadership experience.
* LEAN and Six Sigma training preferred.
* Experience implementing LEAN Manufacturing projects.
* Proficient in use of software - CAD (SolidWorks), MS Project, MS Office, etc.
* Strong problem solving / analytical skills including identifying potential problems and developing effective solutions.
* Demonstrated Leadership skills.
* Minimal travel

records.title: Director, Sourcing and Production, Robert Graham (Menswear)

postedPay.title: Director, Sourcing and Production, Robert Graham (Menswear)

records.description:
**About Us**
Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. Centric Brands is focused on our customers and our brands that will drive the company’s future growth. We are defined by innovation as we seize new opportunities and thrive in an environment informed by creativity and thinking that is both analytical and outside the box. Centric Brands reflects a team built on respect, for others and for the ha rd work it takes to achieve our goals and build our bright future together.
 
 
**Product Development**
From sourcing raw material s to manufacturing, order placement, pricing, quality control and getting the finished product where it needs to be, our production/product development team is responsible for ensuring we keep our standards high and our business profitable at every step of the journey. If you are a focused, results-driven, tenacious and highly flexible team player, we’ll give you every opportunity to build a rewarding career with one of the world’s foremost major lifestyle brand collectives.
 
 
**Specific Responsibilities Would Include**
The Director, Sourcing and Product Development reports to the VP of Production for Robert Graham/Saks and will drive seasonal product initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams, including Production, Design, Sales, and Overseas Offices, to develop and execute assigned product lines. The role primarily focuses on apparel development, with additional responsibility for trims and packaging across Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue Private Label.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and manage all aspects of the product development process, from concept and inspiration through quality assurance of finished goods to the end customer.
* Establish shared qualities and fabrics between Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue to ensure alignment across brands.
* Partner closely with overseas hubs and vendor teams to ensure understanding of departmental objectives and leverage vendor capabilities to drive initiatives that expand competencies as needed.
* Analyze product costs, identifying opportunities and collaborating cross-functionally to create solutions through product engineering that maximize product value while accounting for cost impact.
* Oversee cross-functional milestone performance; communicate risks, deadlines, and business impacts when deliverables are at risk.
* Lead vendor sourcing initiatives aligned with driving innovation and service within the overall sourcing strategy.
* Manage new vendor onboarding and ensure all internal partners are connected and prepared to support production needs.
* Facilitate vendor meetings to review in-season development, production, and delivery challenges, and drive solutions.
* Identify business risks and opportunities, escalate appropriately, and propose actionable recommendations for improvement.
* Collaborate closely with Design and Merchandising on product creation from concept to execution, utilizing budget and SKU plans.
* Create and maintain comprehensive material and product libraries with detailed product attributes and testing documentation.

**Our Best Fit Candidate Would Have**

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); advanced Adobe, Photoshop and Illustrator skills required
* SAP experience preferred
* Excellent organizational, written, and verbal communication skills
* Strong team orientation and ability to work cross-functionally
* Ability to multitask, prioritize, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
* High attention to detail and accuracy
* Knowledge of garment manufacturing, construction, and fabrication

Salary Range: $125,000 - $145,000
 
 
At Centric Brands, we believe our people are our greatest asset, and we seek to structure competitive compensation offers to ensure that we are able to attract and retain the best talent. Our job postings include an annual base salary range at the time of employment. The stated base salary range represents our good faith estimate as to what candidates are likely to expect, and we tailor our offers within the range based on several factors, including the selected candidate's educational and professional experience, industry knowledge, location, technical and communication skills, and other factors that may prove relevant during the selection process. Base salary is a part of a total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, annual bonus and other Centric Brands sponsored benefit programs.
 
 
**Be part of our growing community by getting involved with groups, teams and initiatives like Be Green, Be Giving, and Be Celebrated.**
**Centric Brands is an Equal Opportunity Employer**
Please note that Centric Brands will only reach out to interview, make an offer of employment or conduct onboarding activities for candidates who have applied through our careers site. When interviewing for a position, the candidate experience will include live interaction, such as a video conference or telephone call, with a Recruiter and/or company employee(s). We will never ask for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process. Be aware of suspicious recruitment activity. If you think you are a victim of an employment scam, you may contact your local law enforcement agency and/or visit the Federal Trade Commission website here: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams .

records.description:
**Director of Continuous Improvement**

* **Director of Continuous Improvement**
* **Greater Charlotte Area**
* **$170,000 to $200,000 + Bonus + Strong Company Benefits**

A leading global industrial manufacturer is seeking a Director of Continuous Improvement to drive operational excellence, Lean transformation, and productivity improvements across multiple manufacturing facilities. Reporting directly to the C-suite, this high-impact leadership role will be responsible for deploying enterprise-wide continuous improvement strategies, developing Lean capabilities, and delivering measurable gains in safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost performance. If you're passionate about building high-performing operations, coaching teams, and leading large-scale Lean transformations, this is an outstanding opportunity to make a lasting impact within a growing international organization.

**Key Responsibilities**
:

* Lead the deployment of Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement strategies across multiple manufacturing sites.
 
 Champion the use of Lean methodologies including Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, Standard Work, SMED, TPM, and Six Sigma tools.
* Support plant leadership teams in identifying and executing operational improvement opportunities.
* Coach and mentor Plant Managers, Operations Leaders, CI Managers, and Production Leaders.
* Develop Lean competencies throughout the organization through training, workshops, and hands-on coaching.
* Support facility footprint optimization, cost reduction programs, and operational strategy deployment.
* Pioneer the implementation of digital manufacturing and Smart Factory technologies.
* Ensure operational excellence principles are embedded into daily management systems and site culture.

**The successful candidate will ideally have**
:

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related discipline,
* 10+ years of experience leading Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement initiatives within a manufacturing environment.
* 8+ years of experience applying Lean methodologies in high-volume industrial or automotive manufacturing operations.
* Proven experience driving measurable improvements in productivity, quality, and cost reduction.
* Certified Six Sigma Black Belt (CSSBB).
* Multi-Site Manufacturing experience

**Desired Skills and Experience**
\* Bachelor's degree in Business, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related discipline,
 
\* 10+ years of experience leading Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement initiatives within a manufacturing environment.
 
\* 8+ years of experience applying Lean methodologies in high-volume industrial or automotive manufacturing operations.
 
\* Proven experience driving measurable improvements in productivity, quality, and cost reduction.
 
\* Certified Six Sigma Black Belt (CSSBB).
 
\* Multi-Site Manufacturing experience

records.description:
**Position Overview:**

As the Regional Senior Manager of Post Production/IQR, you will have the unique opportunity to partner closely with several different teams at multiple sites (including IC leadership, reconditioning, and support teams) to drive the strategy behind the development and deployment of Post Production & Quality programs, as well as manage continued performance of internal and external vendors. We are looking for a resourceful self-starter who will set the tone for the successful and fast-paced growth of our Inspection Centers. The Regional Senior Manager of Post Production/IQR role will be heavily focused on leading our teams to effectively close operational gaps and establishing standardized practices that will drive exceptional quality.

**What you'll be doing:**

* Driving successful execution amongst our Post Production teams by effectively leading and developing team members and creating and implementing new processes and systems.
* Identifying issues or roadblocks to execution and quickly taking action to problem solve and implement effective solutions across a large and quickly evolving platform.
* Providing clear direction and necessary support to ensure operational gaps are being closed in a timely manner.
* Working with key business partners to develop systems, metrics, reporting, and staffing models for our Post Production processes and teams.
* Effectively leading and developing onsite personnel at third-party production locations.
* Managing quality of internal and external vendors responsible for producing units for Carvana.
* Establishing effective working relationships with internal and external partners.
* Creating and successfully executing large-scale change management initiatives and new process rollouts.
* Other duties as assigned.

**What the job requires:**

To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

* Minimum of 8 years of leadership, people development, and operations experience
* Experience working in a Lean Manufacturing environment
* Experience developing effective and scalable operating systems and processes
* Proven track record of production process improvement and innovation
* Proven track record of managing complex change across large teams
* Proven track record of leading and developing others
* Proven ability to obtain project deliverables and company metrics
* Strong analytical thinking and organizational skills
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; Ability to learn quickly and transfer knowledge
* Requires standing for extended periods of time with frequent stretching, reaching, walking, stooping, pushing, and/or pulling in an environment that may be cold, hot, noisy, and wet and may have fumes or odors due to vehicle maintenance
* Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.
* Ability to travel up to 80% (multi site responsibility)
* Ability to provide valuable and actionable feedback
* Proficient computer skills
* Must be at least 18 years of age
* Valid driver's license with a clean driving record (no DUIs and no more than two moving violations in the last 3 years).
* Ability to read, write, speak and understand English

This job description is not designed to contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Compensation Range: $120K-$140K annually

**Legal stuff** 
Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. 
Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer. All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law. Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

Please note this job description is not designed to contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.
